p.seg: Miscellaneous Matters, Section One
In the past, Shùn personally engaged in farming, pottery, and fishing, while embodying filial piety and brotherly love.
His father, Gǔsǒu, was stubborn,
his mother was ignorant, and his younger brother, Xiàng, was arrogant.
All were incorrigibly foolish.
Shùn exhausted the way of filial piety
in order to support Gǔsǒu.
Gǔsǒu and Xiàng plotted to dig a well and plaster a granary,
intending to kill Shùn.
Shùn’s filial piety became even more earnest.
When going to the fields, he would wail and weep.
At fifty years old,
he still yearned like an infant.
He can be called the epitome of filial piety.
Therefore, when he farmed at Mount Lì,
the farmers of Mount Lì yielded the boundaries of their fields;
when he made pottery on the banks of the Hé River,
the potters of the Hé River
did not make inferior vessels;
when he fished at Léizé Lake,
the fishermen of Léizé shared their catch equally.
And when he became the Son of Heaven,
the world was transformed by him.
The barbarian tribes all submitted.
To the north, he reached Qú Sōu,
He pacified Jiāozhǐ in the south,
and none did not admire righteousness,
with unicorns and phoenixes in the suburbs.
Therefore, Confucius said:
"The utmost in filial piety and fraternal love
penetrates to the spirits and gods,
and shines upon the four seas."
This speaks of Shùn.
Confucius was in his district and village,
earnestly practicing filial piety,
and residing in Quēdǎng.
The children of Quēdǎng farmed and fished,
and when dividing the catch, those with parents received more,
because he transformed them through filial piety.
Therefore, seventy-two disciples came from afar,
submitting to his virtue.
In Lǔ, there was a man named Shěn Yóushì,
who fed his sheep until they were full in the morning,
in order to deceive the market people.
Gōng Shènshì had a wife who was promiscuous.
Shèn Kuìshì was extravagant, arrogant, and dissolute.
Those in the Lǔ market who sold cattle and horses were skilled at pre-bargaining.
When Confucius was about to become the Minister of Justice of Lǔ,
Shěn Yóushì dared not feed his sheep in the morning,
Gōng Shènshì divorced his wife,
Shèn Kuìshì crossed the border and moved away,
those in Lǔ who sold horses and cattle did not pre-bargain,
but displayed the correct price to wait for customers.
Since he became the Minister of Justice (司寇, Sīkòu),
the Jì (季), Mèng (孟), and Dōu (郈) families destroyed the walls of Féi (費),
and the people of Qí (齊) returned the territory they had invaded from Lǔ (魯).
This was all brought about by accumulating righteousness.
Therefore, it is said:
"When his person is upright,
he is obeyed without giving orders."
When Sūn Shū'áo (孫叔敖) was an infant,
he went out for a walk
and saw a two-headed snake.
He killed it and buried it,
then returned home and wept.
His mother asked him the reason,
and Shū'áo (叔敖) replied, saying:
"I have heard that whoever sees a two-headed snake will die.
Just now, I saw one.
I am afraid I will leave my mother and die."
His mother said:
"Where is the snake now?"
He said:
"Fearing that others might see it again,
I killed and buried it."
His mother said:
"I have heard that those who have hidden virtue,
Heaven repays with blessings.
You will not die."
When he grew up,
he became the Chancellor of Chǔ (楚).
Even before he governed, the people of the state trusted in his benevolence.
Yǔ (禹) rose to prominence through Túshān (塗山).
Jié's downfall was due to Mòxǐ,
Tāng's rise was due to Yǒushēn,
Zhòu's downfall was due to Dájǐ,
Wén and Wǔ's rise was due to Rènsì,
King Yōu's downfall was due to Bāosì.
Therefore, the *Book of Poetry* rectifies "Guān Jū,"
and the *Spring and Autumn Annals* praises Bójī.
Fán Jī
was the consort of the state of Chǔ.
King Zhuāng of Chǔ dismissed the court and feasted late,
and she asked the reason for it.
King Zhuāng said:
"This morning I spoke with a wise prime minister,
and didn't realize the day was so late."
Fán Jī said:
"Who is this wise prime minister?"
The King said:
"It is Yúqiū Zǐ."
Fán Jī covered her mouth and laughed,
and the king asked the reason for it.
She said:
"I am fortunate to be able to hold the towel and comb to serve the King,
It wasn't that she didn't want exclusive honor and affection,
but she thought it would harm the king's righteousness,
so she recommended several people to the same rank as concubines.
Now, Yúqiū Zǐ has been prime minister for decades,
but has never recommended a single worthy.
To know and not recommend
is disloyal;
to not know
is unwise.
How can he be considered worthy?"
The next morning at court,
the king told Yúqiū Zǐ about Fán Jī's words.
Yúqiū Zǐ bowed his head and said,
"It is as Fán Jī says."
Therefore,
he resigned his position and recommended Sūn Shū'áo.
Sūn Shū'áo became prime minister of Chǔ,
and ultimately King Zhuāng became hegemon,
in which Fán Jī played a part.
During the time of Duke Líng of Wèi,
Qú Bóyù was worthy but not employed,
while Mí Zixiá was unworthy but given responsibilities.
The Wèi grandee Shǐ Qiū worried about this,
and repeatedly advised Duke Líng but was not listened to.
Shǐ Qiū fell ill and was about to die,
and said to his son,
"When I die,
hold the funeral in the north hall.
That I could not promote Qū Bóyù and demote Mí Zǐxiá
means I could not rectify the ruler.
One who in life cannot rectify the ruler
should not have a proper funeral after death.
Placing my corpse in the north hall
will be sufficient for me."
Shǐ Qiū died.
Líng Gōng went to offer condolences.
Seeing the funeral in the north hall,
he asked the reason.
His son explained his father's words to Líng Gōng in detail.
Líng Gōng was startled and changed his expression.
He suddenly realized his error and left his seat,
saying,
"When the master was alive, he wished to promote the worthy and demote the unworthy,
and he did not slacken even in death.
Moreover, he used his corpse to remonstrate.
He can be called loyal and unwavering."
Thereupon,
he summoned Qū Bóyù and promoted him to be a minister.
He demoted Mí Zǐxiá,
moved the funeral to the main hall,
completed the proper rites, and then returned.
The state of Wèi became well-governed.
Shǐ Qiū's courtesy name was Zǐyú.
He is the one referred to in the *Analects* as "How upright is Shǐ Yú!"
The ruler of Jìn asked,
"Who can be appointed as successor?"
Qí Xī replied,
The senior minister of Jìn, Qí Xī, was old.
"Xiè Hú is suitable."
The ruler said,
"Isn't he your enemy?"
He replied,
"Your Majesty asked about suitability,
not about enemies."
Jìn then appointed Xiè Hú.
Later, he asked again,
"Who can be appointed as the national military officer?"
Qí Xī replied,
"Wǔ is suitable."
The ruler said,
"Isn't he your son?"
He replied,
"Your Majesty asked about suitability,
not about my son."
The noble men said that Qí Xī was able to recommend the worthy.
He recommended his enemy
without flattery;
he established his son
without favoritism.
The *Book* says:
“Not partial, not partisan,
the Kingly Way is broad and open.”
This describes Qí Xī.
In external appointments, he did not avoid personal enemies;
in internal appointments, he did not favor relatives.
He can be said to have been supremely impartial.
Because he valued goodness, he could promote those of a similar kind.
The *Book of Odes* says:
“Because he possesses it,
therefore he resembles it.”
Qí Xī possessed this quality.
King Gòng of Chǔ was ill,
and summoned his Prime Minister, saying:
“Cháng Shì Guǎn Sū served me,
he always loyally guided me with principle,
and corrected me with righteousness.
When I am with him,
I am uneasy;
when I don't see him,
I miss him.
However,
I have gained something from him;
his contribution is not small,
I must reward him generously.
Shēn Hóu Bó served me,
he always indulged me.
What I delight in,
he encourages me to do;
what I favor,
he is the first to wear;
when I am with him,
I am happy;
when I don't see him,
I am distressed.
Nevertheless,
I will ultimately gain nothing,
his transgression is not small,
I must quickly send him away."
The *Lìngyǐn* said,
"Yes!"
The next day,
the king died.
The *Lìngyǐn* immediately appointed Guǎnsū as Senior Minister,
and expelled Shēn Hóubó from the borders.
Zēngzǐ said,
"When a bird is about to die,
its cry is mournful;
when a person is about to die,
their words are good."
These words revert to their original nature;
this is what they call Gòng Wáng.
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ said,
"If one hears the Dao in the morning,
one can die in the evening."
How can one hear of posterity,
awaken to the next life?
It is still better than disappearing without ever awakening.
In the past, Wèi Wǔhóu 魏武侯 planned an affair and it was fitting,
none of the assembled officials could match it.
He appeared in court with a happy countenance.
Wú Qǐ 吳起 stepped forward and said,
"Has Your Highness heard something of the words of Chǔ Zhuāngwáng 楚莊王?"
Wǔhóu 武侯 said,
"Not yet.
What were the words of Zhuāngwáng 莊王?"
Wú Qǐ 吳起 said,
"Chǔ Zhuāngwáng 楚莊王 planned an affair and it was fitting,
none of the assembled officials could match it.
He appeared in court with a worried countenance.
Shēn Gōng Wūchén 申公巫臣 stepped forward and said,
'Your Majesty appears in court with a worried countenance,
why is that?'
Zhuāngwáng 莊王 said,
'I have heard that,
of the feudal lords, the one who chooses his own teacher becomes a king,
the one who chooses his own friends becomes a hegemon,
and the one who thinks he is sufficient and none of his officials can match him, will perish.
Now, with my unworthy lack of talent,
when I deliberate in court,
and none of the assembled officials can match my judgment,
"Our state is perhaps on the verge of ruin.
That is why I have a worried expression."
What King Zhuang was worried about,
but you alone have a happy expression,
why is that?"
Marquis Wu hesitated and apologized, saying:
"Heaven has sent you, Master, to correct my faults,
Heaven has sent you, Master, to correct my faults!"
The state of Wei banished Duke Xian.
Duke Dao of Jin said to Shi Kuang:
"The people of Wei expelled their ruler,
is that not excessive?"
He replied:
"Perhaps their ruler was indeed excessive.
For Heaven gives birth to the people and establishes a ruler for them,
to have him oversee and shepherd them,
and not let them lose their nature.
A good ruler will reward good and remove the people's troubles,
love the people like his own children,
cover them like Heaven,
and contain them like Earth.
The people support their ruler,
love him like their parents,
look up to him like the sun and moon,
respect him like the spirits,
and fear him like thunder.
"The ruler,
is the master of the spirits,
and the hope of the people.
Heaven loves the people deeply;
how could it allow one person to be unrestrained above the people,
indulging in their lusts,
and abandoning the nature of Heaven and Earth?
It surely would not.
If you oppress the people's nature,
diminish the sacrifices to the spirits,
the common people will lose hope,
and the state will be without a master,
what use will it be then!
What is the point of not removing him?"
The Duke said:
"Good!"
When Zhào Jiǎnzi ascended the Yángcháng slope,
all the ministers bared their shoulders and pushed the chariot,
but Hǔ Huì alone carried his halberd, walked and sang, and did not push the chariot.
Jiǎnzi said:
"I am ascending the slope,
all the ministers are pushing the chariot,
but Huì alone carries his halberd, walks and sings, and does not push the chariot.
This means that Huì, as a minister, is insulting his lord.
As a minister insulting his lord,
what is his crime?"
Hǔ Huì replied,
"Those who, as ministers, insult their ruler
deserve to die and die again."
Jiǎn Zǐ said,
"What does it mean to 'die and die again'?"
Hǔ Huì said,
"Their body dies,
and their wife and children also die.
This is what is meant by 'die and die again.'
You have already heard the crime of a minister who insults his ruler;
have you also heard of a ruler who insults his ministers?"
Jiǎn Zǐ said,
"What is it like for a ruler to insult his ministers?"
Hǔ Huì replied,
"For a ruler to insult his ministers means
the wise will not offer counsel,
the eloquent will not be sent as envoys,
and the brave will not fight.
If the wise do not offer counsel,
then the state is endangered;
if the eloquent are not sent as envoys,
then diplomatic missions will fail;
if the brave do not fight,
then the borders will be invaded."
Jiǎn Zǐ said,
"Good!"
Thereupon he dismissed the assembled ministers,
and did not have his carriage pushed;
He prepared wine for the scholar-officials,
and drank with the assembled ministers,
giving Hǔ Huì the seat of honor.
1.10 Formerly, Zhōu Shě served Zhào Jiǎnzǐ,
Formerly, Zhōu Shě served Zhào Jiǎn Zǐ.
standing at Zhào Jiǎnzǐ's gate
for three days and three nights.
Jiǎnzǐ sent someone out to ask him, saying:
"What is it, sir, that you would instruct me with?"
Zhōu Shě said:
"I wish to be an outspoken minister,
holding a brush and tablet,
following behind you, my lord,
recording your transgressions and writing them down,
so that there are records daily,
results monthly,
and gains yearly."
Jiǎnzǐ was pleased with this
and kept him nearby.
Before long, Zhōu Shě died,
and Jiǎnzǐ gave him a grand burial.
Three years later,
he was drinking merrily with the various grandees,
when Jiǎnzǐ wept.
The grandees rose and went out, saying:
"We, your servants, have committed a capital crime,
without even knowing it."
Jiǎn Zǐ said:
"Grand Masters rebel,
though without guilt.
Formerly, my friend Zhōu Shě had a saying:
'The hides of a hundred sheep
are not as valuable as the fur under one fox's armpit;
the 'yes-yes' of the multitude
is not as good as Zhōu Shě's outspokenness.
Formerly, Zhòu was muddle-headed and perished,
while Wǔ Wáng was outspoken and prospered.'
Since Zhōu Shě's death,
I have never heard of my faults.
Therefore, if a ruler does not hear his errors or hears them but does not correct them, he will perish.
My state is nearly doomed,
and that is why I weep."
Wèi Wén Hóu was sitting with his officers,
and asked,
"What kind of ruler am I?"
The courtiers all said,
"You,
are a benevolent ruler."
When it came to Dí Huáng,
he said,
"You,
are not a benevolent ruler."
Wèi Wén Hóu said,
"How do you explain this?"
He replied:
"When you attacked Zhōngshān 中山,
you did not use the fief to enfeoff your younger brother,
but used it to enfeoff your eldest son.
From this, I know that you are not a benevolent ruler."
Wén Hóu 文侯 became angry and banished Dí Huáng 翟黃.
Huáng 黃 got up and left.
Next was Rèn Zuò 任座.
Wén Hóu 文侯 asked:
"What kind of ruler am I?"
Rèn Zuò 任座 replied:
"You
are a benevolent ruler."
He said:
"How do you explain this?"
He replied:
"I have heard that
when the ruler is benevolent, his ministers are upright.
Just now, Dí Huáng's 翟黃 words were upright.
From this, I know that you
are a benevolent ruler."
Wén Hóu 文侯 said:
"Good!"
He recalled Dí Huáng 翟黃,
and appointed him as Senior Minister.
Zhōngháng Yín 中行寅 was about to die,
so he summoned his chief priest and wanted to accuse him of a crime.
He said:
"You perform sacrifices for me,
are the sacrificial animals not plump and rich?
Furthermore, are your purifications and abstinences not reverent?
What is the reason for the downfall of my state?"
The priest Jiǎn 簡 replied:
"In the past, my former lord, Zhōngháng Mùzǐ 中行穆子,
had only ten leather chariots,
and he did not worry about their inadequacy,
but worried about the inadequacy of virtue and righteousness.
Now, my lord, you have a hundred armored chariots,
and you do not worry about the inadequacy of virtue and righteousness,
but only worry about the inadequacy of chariots.
When boats and chariots are ornamented,
then taxes and levies are heavy;
when taxes and levies are heavy, then the people resent and curse.
Moreover, if you truly believe that prayers are beneficial to the state,
then curses will also cause harm,
generation after generation, the state will perish.
One person prays for it,
and the whole country curses it;
one prayer cannot overcome ten thousand curses,
and the state perishes,
is that not fitting?
What crime has the priest committed?"
Zhōngháng Zǐ 中行子 was then ashamed.
When Qín 秦 desired to attack Chǔ 楚,
they sent an envoy to observe the treasures of Chǔ 楚.
The King of Chǔ 楚 heard of this
and summoned the Chancellor Zǐ Xī 子西 and asked him,
saying:
"Qín 秦 desires to observe the treasures of Chǔ 楚.
Our Hé Shì Zhī Bì 和氏之璧 jade,
the Zhū of Suí Hóu 隨侯之珠,
can we show them these?"
The Chancellor Zǐ Xī 子西 answered,
"I do not know."
He summoned Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 and asked him.
Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 answered,
"This is to observe the gains and losses of our state and to plan against it.
It is not about the treasures;
it is about the worthy ministers.
Pearls, jades, and playthings
are not the most precious things."
The king then sent Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 to respond to them.
Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 dispatched three hundred elite soldiers
and arrayed them inside the Western Gate.
He prepared one altar facing east,
four altars facing south,
and one altar facing west.
When the envoy of Qín 秦 arrived,
Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 said:
"Jūn,
you are a guest,
please take the superior seat facing east."
The Chief Minister Zǐxī faced south,
Grand Clan Elder Zǐ'áo was next in order,
Lord Yè Zǐgāo was next in order,
the Minister of War Zǐfǎn was next in order.
Zhāo Xīxù took his place on the western side of the altar,
and said:
"The guest wishes to see the treasures of the state of Chǔ,
what the state of Chǔ treasures are its virtuous ministers.
To govern the people,
to fill the granaries,
and to enable the people to obtain what they need,
the Chief Minister Zǐxī is here;
to present jade tablets,
to envoy to the feudal lords,
to resolve the difficulty of resentments,
to cultivate joy between the two states,
to ensure there are no worries of war,
Grand Clan Elder Zǐ'áo is here;
to guard the borders,
to be cautious of the boundaries,
not to invade neighboring countries,
and neighboring countries also do not suffer invasion,
Lord Yè Zǐgāo is here;
to manage the armies,
to prepare the weapons,
To face a powerful enemy,
to raise the drumstick and beat the drum,
to mobilize a million troops,
to command all to rush into boiling water and fire,
to tread upon gleaming blades,
to emerge from difficulties where ten thousand deaths are risked for a single chance of survival—
Sīmǎ Zǐfǎn is here for this;
harboring the remaining plans of a hegemon king,
managing the remaining customs of governing amidst chaos,
Zhāo Xīxù is here for this.
They are the object of attention for great states."
The Qin envoy, alarmed, had nothing to say in response.
Zhāo Xīxù then bowed and departed.
The Qin envoy returned,
and said to the Qin ruler:
"Chǔ has many capable ministers,
it is not yet advisable to attack them."
Consequently, they did not attack Chǔ.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"A multitude of accomplished scholars,
King Wén was made tranquil by them."
This is what it means.
Duke Píng of Jìn desired to attack Qí and
sent Fàn Zhāo to observe them.
Duke Jǐng gave him wine as a gift.
In his cups,
Fàn Zhāo said:
"I would like to request a drink from your wine vessel, my lord."
The Duke said:
"Pour from my vessel,
and offer it to the guest."
Fàn Zhāo finished his drink.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Remove the vessel,
and change it!"
The wine vessel and cup were prepared.
Fàn Zhāo feigned drunkenness and, displeased, arose to dance,
and said to the Grand Music Master:
"Can you perform the music of Chéngzhōu for me?
I will dance it for you."
The Grand Music Master said:
"Your humble servant is not familiar with it."
Fàn Zhāo quickly left.
Duke Jǐng said to Yàn Zǐ:
"Jìn
is a great state.
When they send envoys,
they will observe our government.
Now you have angered the envoy of a great state,
what will we do?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"This Fàn Zhāo,
is not ignorant and unacquainted with propriety.
He merely wishes to test our ruler and ministers,
gù jué zhī yě." Therefore, he severed relations with him.
Jǐng Gōng wèi tàishī yuē: "
Zǐ hé yǐ bù wèi kè tiáo Chéngzhōu zhī yuè hū?" Duke Jing said to the Grand Music Master: "Why don't you tune the music of Cheng Zhou for the guest?"
Tàishī duì yuē: "
Fū Chéngzhōu zhī yuè,
tiānzǐ zhī yuè yě,
ruò tiáo zhī,
bì rén zhǔ wǔ zhī.
Jīn Fàn Zhāo rén chén yě,
ér yù wǔ tiānzǐ zhī yuè,

chén gù bù wéi yě." The Grand Music Master replied: "The music of Cheng Zhou is the music of the Son of Heaven. If I were to tune it, it would certainly be the ruler of men who would dance to it. Now, Fàn Zhāo is a subject, and he wishes to dance to the music of the Son of Heaven; therefore, I will not do it."
Fàn Zhāo guī,
yǐ gào Píng Gōng yuē:
"Qí wèi kě fá yě,
chén yù shì qí jūn,
ér Yàn Zǐ shí zhī;
chén yù fàn qí lǐ,

ér tàishī zhī zhī." Fàn Zhāo returned and reported to Duke Ping, saying, "Qi is not yet ready to be attacked. I wanted to test their ruler, and Yàn Zǐ recognized it; I wanted to violate their propriety, and the Grand Music Master knew it."
Zhòngní wén zhī yuē:
"Fū bù chū yú zūn zǔ zhī jiān,
ér zhī qiānlǐ zhī wài,
qí Yàn Zǐ zhī wèi yě,
kěwèi zhéchōng yǐ,

ér tàishī qí yǔ yān." Confucius heard of this and said, "Indeed, without leaving the wine cups and stands, he knows what is happening a thousand miles away. That is what Yàn Zǐ is like. He can be said to ward off attacks, and the Grand Music Master is involved in this as well."
Jìn Píng Gōng fú Xī Hé,
zhōng liú ér tàn yuē:
"Alas!
Where can I find worthy scholars to share this joy with?"
The boatman, Gù Sāng, replied,
"Your words are excessive.
For swords are produced in Yuè,
pearls are produced in the Jiāng and Hàn rivers,
jade is produced on Mount Kūn,
these three treasures,
all arrive without feet.
Now, if you truly cherish scholars,
then worthy scholars will arrive!"
Píng Gōng said,
"Gù Sāng, come here!
I have more than three thousand retainers under my gate.
If morning provisions are insufficient,
I collect market taxes in the evening;
if evening provisions are insufficient,
I collect market taxes in the morning.
Can I still be said to not cherish scholars?"
Gù Sāng replied,
"Now, the swan flies high, soaring into the sky,
but what it relies on is only its six wing feathers.
As for the down on its belly
and the fur on its back,
whether you add or remove a handful,
its flight will not be affected.
I wonder, of your three thousand retainers, are they wing feathers,
or are they down and fur?"
Píng Gōng remained silent and did not respond.
Chǔ Wēi Wáng asked Sòng Yù,
"Does the Master perhaps have some unusual conduct?
Why is it that the scholars and common people do not praise him very much?"
Sòng Yù replied,
"Yes,
indeed,
there is.
I hope that Your Majesty will pardon my offense
and allow me to finish my explanation.
There was a guest who sang in Yǐng zhōng.
At first, he sang 'Xiàlǐ Bārén' (Lowland Commoner),
and those in the capital who joined in and harmonized numbered in the thousands.
When he sang 'Yánglíng Cǎiwēi' (Gathering Ferns on Yánglíng),
those in the capital who joined in and harmonized numbered in the hundreds.
When he sang 'Yángchūn Báixuě' (Sunshine and White Snow),
those in the capital who joined in and harmonized numbered only in the tens.
When he drew out the shāng notes, carved the jiǎo notes,
and mixed in flowing zhǐ notes,
those in the capital who joined in and harmonized
were no more than a few.
It is the case that the higher the tune,
the fewer harmonize with it.
Thus, among birds there is the phoenix, and among fish there is the whale.
The phoenix soars upward to nine thousand miles,
piercing through the floating clouds,
Bearing the azure sky on its back,
soaring above the deep darkness.
How can the quail of the dung-heap field,
possibly fathom the height of heaven and earth with it?
The whale sets out at dawn from the ruins of Kūnlún,
exposes its dorsal fin at Jiéshí,
and rests in the evening at Mèngzhū;
how can the newt of the foot-wide pond,
possibly measure the greatness of rivers and seas with it?
Therefore, it is not only birds that have the phoenix and fish that have the whale,
scholars also have their equivalents.
The sage's extraordinary thoughts and unusual actions,
standing aloof and dwelling alone,
how can the common people of the world,
possibly know what I am doing?"
Duke Píng of Jìn was dwelling in leisure,
and Shī Kuàng was sitting in attendance.
Duke Píng said:
"You were born without eyeballs,
how exceedingly dark are you!"
Shī Kuàng replied:
"There are five forms of darkness in the world,
and I cannot be counted among them."
Duke Píng said:
"What are they?"
Shī Kuàng said:
"The assembled ministers offer bribes to acquire reputations;
the common people suffer injustices,
with nowhere to appeal,
and the ruler is not aware,
this is the first *mò mò*.
Loyal ministers are not employed,
those employed as ministers are not loyal;
inferior talents occupy high positions,
the unworthy oversee the worthy,
and the ruler is not aware,
this is the second *mò mò*.
Treacherous ministers deceive and cheat,
emptying the state treasury,
using their petty talents
to cover up their wickedness,
virtuous men are driven away,
the treacherous and evil are esteemed,
and the ruler is not aware,
this is the third *mò mò*.
The country is poor and the people are exhausted,
superiors and inferiors are not in harmony,
yet (the ruler) is fond of acquiring wealth and using the military,
with insatiable desires,
flatterers
obsequiously at his side,
and the ruler is not aware,
this is the fourth *mò mò*.
The ultimate Way is not clear,
When laws are not enforced,
officials and the people are not upright,
the common people are not at peace,
and the ruler is not aware,
these are the five blacknesses.
If a state has these five blacknesses and is not in danger,
there has never been such a case.
My blackness,
is but a small blackness,
how can it harm the state?"
Zhào Wénzǐ asked Shū Xiàng, saying:
"Of the six generals of Jìn,
who will be the first to perish?"
He replied:
"It will be the Zhōngháng family!"
Wénzǐ said:
"Why will they be the first to perish?"
He replied:
"The way the Zhōngháng family governs
is to treat harshness as discernment,
deceit as intelligence,
severity as loyalty,
many schemes as goodness,
and gathering wealth as excellence.
It is like tanned leather:
it may be large,
It is the way to dismember,
and should have been discarded by the late king."
After King Zhuāng of Chǔ had punished the bandit of Duke Líng of Chén,
killed Xià Zhēngshū,
obtained Xià Jī and was pleased with her,
intending to get close to her.
Shēn Gōng Wūchén advised, saying:
"This woman brought chaos to the state of Chén,
ruined its ministers,
a favored woman should not be approached."
King Zhuāng followed his advice.
The Prime Minister then wanted to take her,
Shēn Gōng Wūchén advised,
and the Prime Minister followed his advice.
Later, Xiāng Yǐn took her,
until King Gōng fought with Jìn at Yānlíng,
the Chǔ army was defeated,
Xiāng Yǐn died,
his corpse was not returned,
repeatedly requesting it from Jìn, but they did not give it.
Xià Jī requested to go to Jìn to seek the corpse,
and Chǔ then sent her.
Shēn Gōng Wūchén was about to be sent as an envoy to Qí,
he privately spoke with Xià Jī,
and plotted with her.
When Xià Jī departed,
Shēn Gōng Wū Chén abandoned his mission,
fled on the road,
and followed Xià Jī to Jìn.
The Chief Minister was about to move his clan,
and reported this to the king, saying:
"Shēn Gōng Wū Chén advised the late king not to get close to Xià Jī,
but now he has abandoned his mission,
and fled to Jìn with Xià Jī,
which is deceiving the late king.
Please move his clan."
The king said:
"Shēn Gōng Wū Chén was loyal in his plans for the late king,
but disloyal in his plans for himself.
This is being generous to the late king while being harsh on himself.
What crime has he committed against the late king?"
So he did not move them.
Miscellaneous Matters, Section Two
In the past, Táng and Yú greatly promoted nine worthies,
placing them in positions,
and the country was greatly peaceful and prosperous,
remote regions came as guests,
and qilin and phoenixes were in the suburbs.
Shāng Tāng employed Yī Yǐn,
and Wén and Wǔ employed Tài Gōng and Hóng Yāo,
Chéng Wáng entrusted Zhōu and Shào,
and the country was greatly governed,
The Yuèshāng people offered double translations,
auspicious omens descended together,
and thus peace prevailed for a thousand years,
all because of the merit of employing the worthy.
Without worthy ministers,
even the Five Emperors and Three Kings
could not rise to prominence.
Duke Huán of Qí obtained Guǎn Zhòng,
and possessed the glory of dominating the feudal lords;
he lost Guǎn Zhòng,
and suffered the disgrace of danger and chaos.
Yú did not employ Bǎilǐ Xī and perished,
Duke Mù of Qín employed him and became a hegemon.
Chǔ did not employ Wǔ Zǐxū and was defeated,
Hélǘ of Wú employed him and became a hegemon,
Fūchāi not only did not employ Zǐxū,
but also killed him,
and his state ultimately perished.
King Zhāo of Yān employed Yuè Yì,
and with the weak troops of Yān,
shattered the strong enemy of Qí,
slaughtering the inhabitants of seventy cities;
but King Huì dismissed Yuè Yì,
replacing him with Qí Jié,
his army was immediately defeated,
and he lost seventy cities:
in this case, the father employed him,
and the son did not,
The matter is visible.
Therefore, Hélǘ rose by employing Zǐxū,
and Fūchā killed him and consequently perished.
Zhāo Wáng prevailed by employing Yuè Yì,
and Huì Wáng drove him away and failed.
These are as clear as black and white.
Qín did not employ Shūsūn Tōng,
and Xiàng Wáng did not employ Chén Píng or Hán Xìn, and both perished.
Hàn employed them and greatly prospered.
This is not long ago.
Alas, the misfortune of losing the worthy is like that,
and the blessing of employing the worthy is like this.
No ruler does not seek the worthy to assist himself,
yet the reason states are thrown into chaos and ruined is
that those so-called "worthy" are not worthy.
Either the ruler makes the worthy act but
discusses it with the unworthy;
or he makes the wise plan it but
consults with the foolish.
The unworthy are jealous of the worthy,
and the foolish are jealous of the wise.
This is why the worthy are obstructed and obscured,
and why they cannot get along for a thousand years.
Either the unworthy employ the worthy but cannot do so for long,
or they do so for long but cannot finish it.
Or unworthy sons dismiss the loyal ministers of their worthy fathers.
The calamities and failures resulting from this are difficult to record one by one.
However, the key lies in the ruler himself being unclear and listening to the multitude.
If slanderous accusations are not acted upon,
that is true discernment.
When Wèi Páng Gōng and the crown prince were hostages in Hándān,
he said to the King of Wèi:
"Now, if one person comes and says there is a tiger in the market,
would Your Majesty believe it?"
The king said,
"No."
He said,
"If two people say so,
would Your Majesty believe it?"
The king said,
"I would be suspicious."
He said,
"If three people say so,
would Your Majesty believe it?"
The king said,
"I would believe it."
Páng Gōng said,
"The fact that there are no tigers in the market is clear.
Three people saying so creates a tiger.
Now, Hándān is farther from Wèi
than the market is;
those who speak ill of me
will exceed three in number.
I hope Your Majesty will investigate this."
King Wei said:
"I know it."
When Páng Gōng returned from Hándān,
slanderous words indeed arrived,
and consequently, he was unable to obtain an audience.
Gān Mào,
a native of Xiàcài,
went west to Qín,
repeatedly rendering meritorious service,
until the time of King Wǔ,
who made him Left Prime Minister,
Chūlǐ Zǐ was made Right Prime Minister.
Chūlǐ Zǐ and Gōngsūn Zǐ
were all princes of Qín,
and their maternal family was from Hán.
They frequently attacked Hán.
King Wǔ of Qín said to Gān Mào:
"I desire to have carriages reach the Zhou royal house,
by the road through Yíyáng of Hán."
He wanted to send Gān Mào to attack Hán,
and seize Yíyáng,
in order to open a road to the Zhou royal house.
Gān Mào said:
"Please make an agreement with Wèi,
to attack Hán together."
He ordered Xiàng Shòu to assist in the journey.
After Gān Mào had made an agreement,
Wèi agreed to Gān Mào.
He returned to Xīrǎng,
and said to Xiàng Shòu:
"You return and tell the king,
Wèi has listened to me,
but I hope the king will not attack."
Xiàng Shòu returned and told the king.
The king greeted Gān Mào at Xīrǎng,
and asked him the reason.
He replied:
"Yíyáng
is a large county;
it is called a county in name,
but in reality, it is a prefecture.
Now, if Your Majesty overcomes several dangerous passes,
and travels a thousand *lǐ* to attack it,
it will be difficult.
In the past,
when Zēng Shēn was in Zhèng,
a person with the same name as Zēng Shēn committed murder.
Someone told his mother,
'Zēng Shēn has committed murder.'
His mother continued weaving as usual.
A little while later,
another person came and told her,
His mother said,
'My son would not commit murder.'
After a while,
another person came to report.
His mother threw down her shuttle and left the loom,
climbed over the wall and ran away.
Even with Zēng Shēn's virtue and his mother's belief in him,
if three people doubted him,
his mother became afraid.
Now, my virtue,
is not comparable to Zēng Shēn's;
Your Majesty's belief in me, your subject,
is also not as great as Zēng Shēn's mother's belief in Zēng Shēn;
those who doubt me are not just three people.
I fear Your Majesty will throw down the shuttle too.
The Marquis Wén of Wèi ordered Yuè Yáng to lead troops to attack Zhōngshān,
and after three years he captured it.
Yuè Yáng returned and spoke of his accomplishments,
Marquis Wén showed him a chest of slanderous writings.
Yuè Yáng bowed twice and kowtowed, saying:
"This is not my achievement,
it is the ruler's power."
Now I am an outsider here,
Chūlǐ Zǐ and Gōngsūn Zǐ,
are colluding with Hán to plot,
Your Majesty will surely believe them,
this would be Your Majesty deceiving Wèi and me bearing the resentment of Hán."
The King said:
"I will not listen."
He ordered an attack on Yíyáng,
but after five months Yíyáng was not yet captured.
Chūlǐ Zǐ and Gōngsūn Zǐ indeed disputed it,
King Wǔ summoned Gān Mào,
wanting to withdraw the troops.
Gān Mào said:
"Xīrǎng is over there."
The King said:
"It is there."
Consequently, he mobilized all the troops,
and appointed Gān Mào as general,
to attack it.
Consequently, he captured Yíyáng.
When King Wǔ died,
and King Zhāo ascended the throne,
Chūlǐ Zǐ and Gōngsūn Zǐ slandered him,
and Gān Mào was convicted,
and eventually fled to Qí.
Therefore, if one is not extremely enlightened,
who can avoid being subjected to slander?
The King of Chǔ asked his ministers:
"I have heard that the north fears Zhāo Xīxù.
Is it truly so?"
Jiāng Yǐ replied:
"A tiger sought to eat all the beasts,
and caught a fox.
The fox said:
"You dare not eat me!
The Heavenly Emperor ordered me to be the leader of all beasts.
Now if you eat me,
you will be defying the Emperor's command.
If you don't believe me,
I will go ahead of you.
You follow behind me.
Watch all the beasts, and none will not run when they see me."
The tiger thought this was true,
and followed it.
The beasts all ran when they saw them.
The tiger did not know that the beasts were afraid of it and ran,
but thought they were afraid of the fox.
Now, Your Majesty, your territory is five thousand *lǐ* square,
and you have a million soldiers,
but you rely solely on Zhāo Xīxù.
The north is not afraid of Zhāo Xīxù,
but in reality is afraid of Your Majesty's armor and weapons,
just as the beasts are afraid of the tiger.
Therefore, when a minister is feared,
it is a reflection of the ruler's power.
If the ruler is not wise enough to use that power,
then the power will be lost."
The ruler of Lǔ sent Mì Zǐjiàn to be the magistrate of Shànfù.
Zǐjiàn resigned,
and then requested to borrow two good scribes,
to have them write the laws and instructions on governing.
The ruler of Lǔ gave them to him.
Upon arriving at Shànfù,
he had them write,
and Zǐjiàn pulled on their elbows from the side.
The writing was ugly,
then he would get angry at him;
if he wanted the writing to be good,
then he would pull at it again.
The scribe worried about this,
asked to resign and leave,
and returned to report to the Lord of Lǔ.
The Lord of Lǔ said:
"Zǐjiàn is distressed that I disturb him,
causing him to be unable to implement his good governance."
So he ordered the officials,
that none should be allowed to arbitrarily levy taxes on Dānfù.
The transformation of Dānfù became greatly ordered.
Therefore, Confucius said:
"What a gentleman is Zǐjiàn!
If Lǔ had no gentlemen,
where would this be obtained!"
He praised his virtue.
A man of Chǔ had a fish presented to the King of Chǔ,
saying:
"Today's fishing catch,
"It cannot be finished by eating,
it cannot be sold,
it is a pity to throw it away,
therefore I have come to offer it."
The attendants around him said:
"How rude the words are!"
Chǔ Wáng said:
"You do not understand the fisherman,
he is a benevolent man.
It has been said that if the granaries have surplus grain,
the state has starving people;
if the rear palace has many secluded women,
the common people have many single men;
if excessive surpluses are stored in the treasury,
the territory has many poor and distressed people.
All these are failures of the way of a ruler.
Therefore, if the kitchen has fat fish,
the stables have fat horses,
the people have hungry faces.
These are the reasons for the downfall of a ruler,
hoarding in treasuries.
I have heard of this for a long time,
but have not been able to put it into practice.
The fisherman knows this,
he is using this to advise me.
Let us implement it now."
Thereupon,
he sent envoys to care for widowers and widows, and to support orphans;
To release grain from the granaries and distribute coins and silk to relieve (the people) was insufficient;
(he) dismissed those women in the harem whom he did not favor,
released them and married them to widowers.
The people of Chǔ were overjoyed,
and neighboring states submitted to him.
Therefore, when a fisherman offered a single surplus fish,
the state of Chǔ relied on it.
This can be called benevolence and wisdom.
In the past, Zōu Jì met with King Xuān of Qí by playing the zither,
and King Xuān approved of it.
Zōu Jì said:
"The zither is therefore a symbol of governance."
Thereupon, he explained to the king how the zither symbolizes governance, as well as matters of hegemony and kingship.
King Xuān was greatly pleased,
and spoke with him for three days.
Consequently, he appointed him as his prime minister.
In Qí, there was a scholar from Jìxià who
liked to discuss political affairs.
After Zōu Jì became prime minister of Qí,
seventy-two people, including the Jìxià scholar Chúnyú Kūn,
all looked down on Zōu Jì,
thinking that he was merely skilled in rhetoric,
and that Zōu Jì could not match them.
So they went together to see Zōu Jì.
Chúnyú Kūn and his followers were arrogant in their manners,
while Zōu Jì's manners were humble.
Chún yú Kūn 淳于髡 and others said:
"A fox-fur (hú bái) robe,
patched with worn sheepskin,
what do you think of that?"
Zōu Jì 鄒忌 said:
"Respectfully agreed!
I dare not mix the worthy with the unworthy."
Chún yú Kūn 淳于髡 said:
"A square inside but a round hub (yuán gāng),
what do you think of that?"
Zōu Jì 鄒忌 said:
"Respectfully agreed!
I will carefully guard the gates,
and dare not detain guests."
Chún yú Kūn 淳于髡 and others said:
"Three men jointly tending one sheep,
the sheep doesn't get to eat,
and the men also don't get to rest,
what do you think of that?"
Zōu Jì 鄒忌 said:
"Respectfully agreed!
Reduce officials and streamline personnel,
so that they do not disturb the people."
Chún yú Kūn 淳于髡 and others stated this three times,
and Zōu Jì 鄒忌 acknowledged it three times as promptly as an echo.
Chún yú Kūn 淳于髡 and others, finding themselves at a loss, departed.
Zōu Jì's 鄒忌 demeanor was arrogant,
while Chún yú Kūn's 淳于髡 demeanor was humble.
故所以尚 Gānjiàng Mòyé zhě,
guì qí lì duàn yě;
suǒyǐ guì qíjì zhě,
wèi qí lì zhì yě.
Bì qiě lì rì kuàng jiǔ hū,
sī lí yóu néng qiè shí,
nú mǎ yì néng zhì yuǎn.
Shì yǐ cōngmíng jié mǐn,
rén zhī měi cái yě.
Zǐgòng yuē:
"Huí yě wén yī yǐ zhī shí."
Měi mǐn jié yě.
Xīzhě,
Yān xiàng dé zuì yú jūn,
jiāng chū wáng,
zhào mén xià zhū dàfū yuē:
"Yǒu néng cóng wǒ chū zhě hū?"
Sān wèn,
zhū dàfū mò duì.
Yān xiàng yuē:
"Xī!
Yì yǒu shì zhī bùzú yǎng yě."
Dàfū yǒu jìn zhě yuē:
"Yì yǒu jūn zhī bùnéng yǎng shì,
ān yǒu shì zhī bùzú yǎng zhě?
Xiōng nián jī suì,
Scholars do not have enough to eat even the dregs of grain,
while your lordships' dogs and horses have surplus grain;
in the depth of winter's bitter cold,
scholars' coarse garments are incomplete,
and their bodies are not covered,
while your lordships' terraces and pavilions
have curtains and draperies of brocade and embroidery,
fluttering in the wind and becoming worn.
Wealth,
is what your lordship takes lightly;
death,
is what scholars value.
If your lordship cannot give what you take lightly,
and seeks to obtain what scholars value,
is that not difficult?"
The Yàn chancellor was then ashamed,
and fled,
not daring to appear again.
Duke Wén of Jìn went out hunting,
the vanguard said:
"Ahead there is a large snake,
as tall as a dike,
blocking the road completely."
Duke Wén said:
"I have heard that
if a feudal lord has a bad dream, then he cultivates virtue,
Dàfū mèng è zé xiū guān,
shì mèng è zé xiū shēn,
If they do so, calamity will not come!
Now, I, the lesser one, have transgressions.
Heaven is warning me,
I shall turn the chariot around and return."
The one driving in front said:
"Your servant has heard it said,
'One who is pleased receives no reward;
one who is angry receives no punishment.'
Now, misfortune or fortune is already before us,
it cannot be changed,
why not just proceed?"
Duke Wén said:
"That is not so.
Spirits cannot overcome the Way,
and demons cannot overcome virtue.
Before misfortune or fortune manifests,
it can still be transformed."
He turned the chariot around and returned.
He fasted for three days,
and prayed in the temple, saying:
"I am young,
the sacrificial animals are not fat,
the gifts are not generous,
that is one fault;
I am fond of hunting with arrows,
without restraint,
The second offense;
I excessively levy taxes and duties,
apply severe punishments,
is the third offense.
I propose that from now on,
there be no tariffs at checkpoints and markets,
no taxes or levies on ponds and weirs,
pardon criminals,
halve the tax on old fields,
and not tax new fields."
Before half a decade had passed since implementing this decree,
the official guarding the snakes dreamt that the great god killed the snake,
and said:
"Why are you obstructing the way of the sage?
Your crime deserves death."
He awoke from the dream,
and saw that the snake was stinking and rotten.
He reported it.
Wén Gōng said:
"Indeed,
spirits ultimately cannot overcome the Way,
and demons also cannot overcome virtue.
Why must we seek deep reasons and submit to fate?
We should respond with virtue alone."

The Lord of Liáng reached out and took his hand,
and took him into the carriage.
Returning,
they entered the temple gate.
He shouted "Long live!" and said:
"Fortunate is today,
others hunt and all obtain birds and beasts,
I hunt and obtain good words and return."
King Wǔ conquered Yīn,
obtained two captives and questioned them,
saying:
"Does your country have omens?"
One captive answered:
"My country has omens,
stars are seen during the day and blood rains down,
these are the omens of my country."
One captive answered:
"These are indeed omens,
however,
they are not the greatest.
The omens of my country,
the greatest of them,
sons do not listen to their fathers,
younger brothers do not listen to their elder brothers,
the ruler's commands are not carried out,
"This is a great demon."
Jìn Wén Gōng 晉文公 went hunting in the fields.
Chasing game,
he lost his way and entered a large marsh,
becoming lost and unable to find his way out.
Among them was a fisherman.
Wén Gōng 晉文公 said to him:
"I
am your lord.
From which way can I exit?
I will richly reward you!"
The fisherman said:
"Your servant wishes to make a contribution."
The duke said:
"First lead me out of the marsh, and then I will accept it."
Thereupon,
he led him out of the marsh.
The duke commanded, saying:
"What is it that you would teach me?
I wish to receive it."
The fisherman said:
"Swans and wild geese dwell in the rivers and seas;
if they grow weary of them and wish to migrate to a small marsh,
they will surely have the worry of nine-stringed arrows.
Turtles and alligators dwell in deep pools;
if they grow weary of them and come out to shallow waters,
then you will surely have the worry of nets, snares, hooks, and arrows.
Now that you, my lord, are chasing game,
and have strayed so far as to enter Dàng,
why have you traveled so far!"
Wén Gōng said,
"Well said!"
He ordered his attendants to record the fisherman's name.
The fisherman said,
"By what are you named, my lord?
If you revere Heaven and serve Earth,
respect the altars of the soil and grain,
secure the four regions,
show compassion and love to the myriad people,
lighten the levies and taxes,
and reduce the land rent,
then your subject is also part of it.
If you do not respect the altars of the soil and grain,
and do not secure the four regions,
outwardly lose propriety towards the feudal lords,
and inwardly go against the people's hearts,
and the country becomes a place of wandering refugees,
then even if a fisherman receives generous gifts,
he will not be able to keep them."
He then declined to accept them,
saying,
"You, my lord, should quickly return to your state,
and I will also return to my fishing grounds."
Jìn Wén Gōng 晉文公 hunted a deer and lost it.
He asked an old farmer, Lǎo Gǔ 老古, saying:
"Where is my deer?"
Lǎo Gǔ 老古 pointed with his foot and said:
"Go that way."
The Duke said:
"I am asking you;
why point with your foot?"
Lǎo Gǔ 老古 shook his clothes and stood up, saying:
"I never imagined a ruler could be like this.
The dwelling place of tigers and leopards
dislikes quiet and prefers to be near people,
therefore they are obtained.
The dwelling place of fish and turtles
dislikes deep water and goes to shallow water,
therefore they are obtained.
The lords who dislike the masses lose their states.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'The magpie has built its nest,
and the dove occupies it.'
You are released and do not return;
people will take over your position."
Thereupon,
Wén Gōng 晉公 was afraid,
and on his way back, he met Luán Wǔzǐ 欒武子.
Luán Wǔzǐ 欒武子 said:
"Did you obtain a beast from the hunt?
and had a pleased expression."
Wén Gōng said,
"I was hunting deer and lost them,
but I gained good words,
therefore I have a pleased expression."
Luán Wǔzǐ said,
"Where is that person?"
Wén Gōng said,
"I did not bring him with me."
Luán Wǔzǐ said,
"To occupy a high position and not care for those below is arrogance;
to issue orders slowly and punish quickly is tyranny;
to take a person's words
and abandon the person himself is robbery."
Wén Gōng said,
"Good!"
He turned back and took Lǎo Gǔ and returned together.
Biǎn Què saw Qí Huán Hóu,
and stood for a while.
Biǎn Què said,
"You have an illness,
it is in the pores,
if you don't treat it, I fear it will become deep."
Huán Hóu said:
"I have no illness."
Biǎn Què left.
Huán Hóu said:
"Doctors are greedy for profit.
They want to treat what isn't an illness to claim credit."
After ten days,
Biǎn Què saw him again,
and said:
"Your illness
is in the skin;
if you don't treat it, it will go deeper."
Huán Hóu did not respond.
Biǎn Què left.
Huán Hóu was displeased.
After ten days,
Biǎn Què saw him again,
and said:
"Your illness
is in the intestines and stomach;
if you don't treat it, it will go deeper."
Huán Hóu did not respond.
Biǎn Què left.
Huán Hóu was again displeased.
After ten days,
Biǎn Què saw him again,
looked at Huán Hóu, and turned and ran.
Huán Hóu sent someone to ask him why.
Biǎn Què said:
"The illness is in the *còulǐ* (skin and muscle),
where decoctions and warming can reach;
it is in the *jīfū* (flesh and skin),
where acupuncture and medicinal stones can reach;
it is in the intestines and stomach,
where strong medicine can reach;
it is in the bone marrow,
where the Arbiter of Fate can do nothing about it.
Now it is in the bone marrow,
therefore, I have nothing to request."
Five days later,
Lord Huán felt pain in his body,
and sent someone to look for Biǎn Què.
Biǎn Què had already fled to Qín.
Lord Huán then died.
Therefore, the good doctor treats illness,
by attacking it in the *còulǐ*.
These matters are all treated when they are small.
As for the misfortune and fortune of events,
there are also places like the *còulǐ*.
Therefore, the sage deals with them early on.
Zhuāng Xīn advised King Xiāng of Chǔ, saying:
"Your Majesty is with Lord Zuǒ Zhōu on the left,
and Lord Xià Hóu on the right,
following Lord Xīn'ān,
"Sharing a carriage with Lord Shòulíng,
indulging in excessive extravagance and waste,
and neglecting affairs of state,
Yǐng is in danger!"
The king said,
"Are you senile, sir?
Are you presumptuously acting as a harbinger of doom for the state of Chǔ!"
Zhuāng Xīn replied,
"Your subject dares not be a harbinger of doom for Chǔ;
I truly see it.
If Your Majesty continues to associate closely with these four men,
then Chǔ will surely perish.
I ask to stay in Zhao to observe it."
Thereupon,
before ten months had passed,
the king indeed lost the lands of Wūshān, Jiānghàn, and Yānyǐng.
Thereupon,
the king then sent for Zhuāng Xīn,
who had gone to Zhao.
When Xīn arrived,
the king said,
"Alas!
You have come, sir!
I have come to this because I did not heed your words.
What is to be done?"
Zhuāng Xīn said,
"If Your Majesty uses my words, then it can be remedied;
if you do not use my words,
it will be even worse than this.
Common people have a saying:
'To mend the sheepfold after losing the sheep
is not too late;
to call the dog after seeing the rabbit
is not too late.'"
Tāng and Wǔ became kings with a hundred *lǐ*,
Jié and Zhòu lost the empire.
Now, although Chǔ is small,
by cutting off the long and continuing the short,
it numbers in the thousands of *lǐ*,
how could it be merely a hundred *lǐ*?
Moreover, does Your Majesty not see the dragonfly?
With six legs and four wings,
it flies between Heaven and Earth,
seeking mosquitoes and gadflies to eat,
at times drinking sweet dew,
thinking itself without worry,
and not contending with the people.
It does not know that a five-foot-tall child
adds a sticky silk pole to it from a height of forty *rèn*,
and below it becomes food for insects and moths.
The dragonfly is still a small thing;
the sparrow bows and pecks at white grains,
looks up and roosts in lush trees,
beats its wings,
and stirs its body,
thinking itself without worry,
yǔ mín wú zhēng yě. Does not contend with the people.
Bù zhī Gōngzǐ Wángsūn, Unaware of the princes and nobles,
zuǒ bǎ dàn, Holding pellets in the left hand,
yòu shè wán, And holding pellets in the right,
dìng cāochí, Certainly in control,
shěn cānlián, Carefully calculating the aim,
gù zhòu yóu hū màoshù, Therefore, during the day they roam among the lush trees,
xī hé hū suān xián. And in the evening, they harmonize with sour and salty flavors.
Jué yóu qí xiǎo zhě yě, Even the sparrow is still a small creature,
hónghú xīyóu hū Jiāng Hàn, While swans and geese play in the Yangtze and Han rivers,
xī liú hū dà zhǎo, Resting and staying in the large marshes,
fǔ zhuó yū lǐ, Bowing to peck at mudfish and carp,
yǎng fèn líng héng, Looking up and striving to ascend the heights,
xiū qí liù hé ér líng qīngfēng, Extending their six wings to soar on the clear wind,
biāoyáo gāo xiáng, Whirling and flying high,
yī jǔ qiānlǐ, Covering a thousand li in a single flight,
zì yǐ wéi wú huàn, Believing themselves to be free from worry,
yǔ mín wú zhēng yě. Not contending with the people.
Bù zhī yì zhě xuǎn qí gōng nǔ, Unaware that archers choose their bows and crossbows,
xiū qí fáng yì, Repairing their blinds and screens,
jiā zēng jiǎo qí jǐng, Adding silken cords to its neck,
tóu hū bǎirèn zhī shàng, Throwing it down from a hundred *rèn* above,
yǐn xiān jiǎo, Pulling the slender cord,
yáng wēi bō, Raising a slight ripple,
zhé qīngfēng ér yǔn. Snapping the clear wind, and causing it to fall.
Gù zhāo yóu hū Jiāng Hé, Therefore, in the morning, they roam in the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers,
ér mù tiáo hū dǐng zǔ. And in the evening, they are seasoned in pots and platters.
Hónghú yóu qí xiǎo zhě yě, Even swans and geese are still small creatures,
Cài hóu zhī shì gù shì yě.
Cài hóu nán yóu hū Gāolíng,
běi jìng hū Wūshān,
Zhú mí jūn zhāng lù,
guò xī zǐ,
suí shí niǎo,
Xī yóu hū Gāocài zhī yòu,
yì mǎn wú yá,
bù yǐ guójiā wéi shì.
Bù zhī Zǐfā shòu lìng Xuān wáng,
è yǐ Huái shuǐ,
tián yǐ Wūshān,
Gēngzǐ zhī cháo,
yīng yǐ zhūsī,
chén ér zòu zhī hū Xuān wáng yě.
Cài hóu zhī shì yóu qí xiǎo yě,
Jīn jūnwáng zhī shì,
suì yǐ Zuǒ Zhōu hóu,
yòu Xià hóu,
cóng Xīn'ān Jūn yǔ Shòulíng Jūn,
yín yǎn chǐ mǐ,
kāng lè yóu yú,
chíchěng hū Yúnmèng zhī zhōng,
bù yǐ tiānxià yǔ guójiā wéi shì,
bù zhī Rǎng hóu fāng yǔ Qín wáng móu,
zhì zhī yǐ Mǐn è,
ér tóu zhī hū Mǐn sài zhī wài."
Ér Xiāng wáng dà jù,
His body trembled and shuddered,
he said:
"I respectfully accept your command."
Thereupon, he enfeoffed Zhuāng Xīn 莊辛 as Lord Chénglíng 成陵君 and employed his strategy,
and together they raised up the twelve lords of the Huáiběi 淮北 region.
Marquis Wèi Wén 魏文侯 went on an excursion,
and saw a traveler wearing a fur coat inside out and carrying grass on his back.
Marquis Wén said:
"Why are you wearing your fur coat inside out and carrying grass?"
He replied:
"I cherish its fur."
Marquis Wén said:
"Don't you know that if the lining is exhausted, the fur will have nothing to rely on?"
The next year, Dōngyáng 東陽 reported its accounts,
and the money and cloth had increased tenfold.
The high officials all congratulated him.
Marquis Wén said:
"This is not something to be congratulated for.
It is no different from the traveler wearing a fur coat inside out and carrying grass.
He wants to cherish its fur,
but does not know that if the lining is exhausted,
the fur will have nothing to rely on.
Now, our fields have not become more extensive,
and our soldiers and people have not become more numerous,
yet the money has increased tenfold,
it must have been taken from the scholar-officials.
I have heard that,
when those below are not at peace,
those above cannot reside securely.
This is not something to congratulate me on."
2.17 King Zhuang of Chu asked Sūn Shū'áo,
"I have not yet grasped what constitutes the proper way to govern the state."
Sūn Shū'áo said,
"That which a state deems correct,
the multitude invariably dislikes.
I fear that Your Majesty will be unable to determine it."
The king said,
"If it cannot be determined,
is it solely the ruler's responsibility?
Or is it also the responsibility of the ministers?"
Sūn Shū'áo said,
"A ruler who is arrogant towards his officers says:
'Without me, officers would have no prosperity or wealth.'
And officers who are arrogant towards their ruler say:
'Without officers,
the state would have no peace or strength.'
Rulers may even lose their states without realizing it,
and officers may suffer hunger and cold without advancing their careers.
When ruler and minister are not in accord,
the proper way to govern the state can never be determined.
Xià Jié and Yīn Zhòu,
did not determine the proper way to govern the state,
To deem as right that which accords with his (the ruler's) likes and dislikes,
and to deem as wrong that which does not accord with his likes and dislikes,
thus leads to ruin without knowing it."
King Zhuang said:
"Excellent!
I wish the prime minister and the lords and senior officials would jointly determine the affairs of the state.
How dare I, with my limited country, be arrogant toward the scholars and people?"
King Zhuang of Chu took the reins of government,
but for three years did not govern,
and was fond of hidden amusements.
The state was in danger,
the country was about to perish.
Shi Qing asked the attendants and ministers on the left and right, saying:
"The king has taken the reins of government,
but for three years has not governed,
and is fond of hidden amusements,
the state is in danger,
the country is about to perish.
Why don't you go and remonstrate?"
The attendants said:
"You should go."
Shi Qing entered,
bowed twice and advanced, saying:
"There is a large bird,
that has come to perch on the south slope of Nanshan Mountain,
for three years it has not flown nor sung,
I don't know what the reason for this is?"
The king said:
"You may leave,
I know about it."
Shi Qing said:
"My words may mean death,
If I do not speak, I will also die.
I wish to hear the explanation."
The King said:
"This bird does not fly,
in order to grow its feathers and wings;
It does not sing,
in order to observe the faults of the ministers.
Although this bird does not fly,
when it flies, it will surely soar into the sky;
Although it does not sing,
when it sings, it will surely startle people."
Shì Qìng bowed his head and said:
"I have received what I wished to hear."
The King was greatly pleased with Shì Qìng's question,
and appointed him as Chief Minister,
and gave him the Prime Minister's seal.
Shì Qìng was pleased,
and went out the door, looked to his left and right, and laughed, saying:
"My King,
is King Chéng."
The Central Attendant heard this,
knelt and wept, saying:
"Your servant has been a courtier in charge of clothing and carriages for thirteen years.
Formerly, I was a sharp arrow,
and later, I became a defensive barrier.
The King bestowed the seal of Prime Minister on Shì Qìng (士慶) but did not bestow it on me.
Your servant's death is approaching!"
The King said,
"I dwell in the mire.
What you discuss with me
does not concern the internal affairs of the state,
nor the external relations with the various lords.
A man like you
can be enriched but not ennobled."
Thereupon,
he took out the treasured jade from the state treasury to bestow upon him,
and said,
"Loyalty and trustworthiness
are the conduct of a scholar;
words
are the path of a scholar.
If the path is not repaired and maintained,
the scholar has nowhere to go."
2.19 Jìngguō Jūn (靖郭君) wanted to fortify Xuē (薛),
and many guests tried to dissuade him.
The Lord told the gatekeeper:
"Do not report any affairs for the guests."
Thereupon,
There was a man of Qi who said:
"I wish to speak one word;
if it is more than one word,
I beg to be boiled."
The usher presented the guest.
The guest said:
"Sea, big fish."
Thereupon, he turned and ran.
Lord Jìng Guō said:
"Please advance a little."
The guest said:
"No,
I dare not trifle with death."
Lord Jìng Guō said:
"Alas,
I have no choice;
try to explain it again."
The guest said:
"Has your Lordship not heard of the big fish in the sea?
Nets cannot stop it,
barbed arrows cannot restrain it;
If Dang loses its waterways and land dwellings,
then ants and termites will be pleased.
Moreover, Qi
is also like water to you, my lord.
Since you already possess Qi,
what use is Xue to you?
If you do not have Qi,
then even building a city at Xue would be of no benefit."
Lord Jing Guo was greatly pleased,
dismissed the people,
and did not build a city at Xue.
2.20 In Qi, there was a woman,
and the state was greatly at peace,
all thanks to the power of the ugly woman.
Miscellaneous Matters, Chapter Three
King Huì of Liáng said to Mencius:
"I have a failing,
I am fond of beauty."
Mèngzǐ said:
"If the King is truly fond of beauty,
what harm is there to the King?"
The King said:
"How can being fond of beauty lead to ruling?"
Mèngzǐ said:
"If the Great King is fond of beauty,
the 《Book of Odes》 says:
'Old Duke Dǎnfǔ,
came to court riding swiftly,
along the banks of the western rivers,
arriving at the foot of Mount Qí,
thus reaching Jiāngnǚ,
then coming to live there together.'
If the Great King loves his consorts,
and always goes in and out with them,
at that time,
there will be no resentful women within,
and no unmarried men without.
If the King is fond of beauty,
and shares it with the people,
The people only fear that the king does not enjoy sensual pleasures!"
The king said,
"I have a problem.
I am fond of bravery."
Mèngzǐ said,
"If the king is fond of bravery,
internally he does not uphold the governance of the state,
this is the fourth danger.
Therefore it is said:
"Danger!
Danger!"
Thereupon,
King Xuān was silently speechless,
his mind entered the Yellow Springs,
suddenly he looked up,
and sighed deeply, saying:
'Painful indeed are the words of Lord Wú Yán,
I now hear for the first time of my own dangers.
My dangers almost went unheeded!'
Thereupon,
he immediately stopped the Jiàn Tái construction,
dismissed the female musicians,
removed the flatterers,
got rid of excessive ornamentation,
selected soldiers and horses,
filled the treasury,
opened the four gates of the palace,
summoned and advanced those who spoke frankly,
and extended his reach to the humble and secluded.
He chose an auspicious day,
to establish the crown prince,
advanced his kind mother,
revealed hidden women,
and appointed Lord Wú Yán as queen,
to the south there is the enmity of powerful Chǔ,
externally there are the troubles from three states,
internally there is a gathering of treacherous ministers,
and the people do not support you.
At the age of forty,
strong men are not established,
he doesn't focus on (producing) many sons but focuses on many women,
he honors what he likes and neglects what he relies on.
Once the mountains and tombs collapse,
the state will be unstable,
this is the first danger.
The Jiàntái (漸臺) has five layers,
(decorated with) gold and white jade,
lánggān (琅玕) and dragon carvings,
kingfisher feathers and pearls,
densely and continuously ornamented,
the people are exhausted,
this is the second danger.
The virtuous hide in the mountains and forests,
flatterers are powerful on the left and right,
wickedness and falsehood stand in the central court,
those who offer remonstrance cannot enter,
this is the third danger.
Wine and drink flow copiously,
continuing the night into the morning,
female musicians and actors,
laugh wildly and unrestrainedly,
externally he does not cultivate the rituals of the feudal lords,
I merely admire Your Majesty's excellent morality."
The King said:
"Even so,
what is there to admire?"
After a long pause, she said:
"I have often admired your concealment."
The King said:
"Concealment,
is indeed what I desire.
Try to practice it."
Before he finished speaking,
she suddenly disappeared.
King Xuān was greatly shocked,
and immediately issued a decree to seek out books on concealment and read them.
He withdrew and pondered it,
but still could not understand.
The next day, he summoned her again to question her,
but she did not respond with concealment.
She only raised her eyes, clenched her teeth,
raised her hand and patted her elbow, saying:
"How dangerous!
How dangerous!"
This happened four times.
King Xuān said:
"I wish to hear your command."
The woman of Wú Yán replied:
"Now, Your Majesty's rule of the country is such that,
to the west there is the threat from Héng and Qín,
she brushed off her coarse garments,
went to King Xuan herself,
and wished for an audience.
She said to the gatekeeper:
am an unsold woman of Qi,
have heard of Your Majesty's sage virtue
and wish to serve in the cleaning of the inner palace.
I kowtow outside the Sīmǎ Gate,
hoping Your Majesty will deign to grant my request."
The gatekeeper reported this.
King Xuān was then holding a banquet on the Jiàn Terrace.
Those around him heard this,
and none did not cover their mouths and laugh loudly, saying:
"This is the most shameless woman in the world."
Thereupon,
King Xuān summoned her and received her,
saying:
"In the past, the late king chose consorts for me,
and all the positions are already filled.
Today, I listen to the music of Zhèng and Wèi,
sighing and feeling sorrow,
and promoting the remaining customs of excitable Chǔ.
Now, madam, you are not tolerated as a commoner in your village,
yet you wish to intrude upon the lord of ten thousand chariots.
Do you have some extraordinary ability?"
The woman of Wúyán replied:
"I have none,
extremely ugly and without equal,
known as the Woman of Wu Yan.
As for her appearance,
she had a mortar-shaped head and deep-set eyes,
was tall, strong, and large-jointed,
with a raised nose and a goiter,
a thick neck and sparse hair,
a bent waist and protruding chest,
and skin like lacquer.
At the age of thirty,
she was nowhere accepted,
advertised for marriage but not sold,
cast off and no one would take her in.
Thereupon,
what difficulty would there be for the king?"
The king said,
"How can being fond of bravery lead to becoming a true king?"
Mèngzǐ said,
"The *Book of Odes* says:
'The king was greatly angry,
and accordingly, he organized his troops,
to stop the departing troops,
to strengthen the support of Zhōu,
and to respond to all under Heaven.'
This was King Wén's bravery.
King Wén was angry once and brought peace to the people of all under Heaven.
Now, if the king were to be angry once and bring peace to the people of all under Heaven,
the people would only fear that the king is not fond of bravery."
3.2 Sūn Qīng and Lín Wǔ Jūn discussed military affairs in front of King Xiàochéng of Zhào.
The king said,
"May I ask about the essentials of military affairs?"
Lín Wǔ Jūn replied,
"Above, one obtains the timing of Heaven;
below, one obtains the advantages of terrain.
後 zhī fā,
先 zhī zhì,
cǐ yòng bīng zhī yàoshù yě."
Sūn Qīng said:
"That is not so.
What I have heard
of the ancient way
is that in all battles,
the art of using troops
lies in unifying the people.
If bows and arrows are not in tune,
Yì cannot hit the mark;
if six horses are not in harmony,
Zàofù cannot drive them far;
if the soldiers and people are not close and attached,
Tāng and Wǔ cannot achieve victory.
Therefore, one who is good at using troops
must strive to be good at attaching the people."
Lín Wǔ Jūn said:
"That is not so.
What is valued in troops is power and advantage;
what is prized is change, deception, attack, and plunder.
One who is good at using them
appears suddenly and swiftly, with no one knowing where they come from.
Sūn and Wú used this,
and were unrivaled in the world.
From this point of view,
is it necessarily essential to wait for the people's attachment?"
Master Sūn said:
"Not so.
What I am talking about
is the army of a true king,
affairs of a ruler;
what you are talking about
is power and profit,
what you value
is change, deceit, attack, and plunder.
The army of a benevolent person
cannot be deceived;
those who can be deceived
are the lazy,
the isolated,
and those between ruler and ministers,
above and below, who have scattered and have different virtues.
If one uses Jié to deceive Jié,
there might still be luck involved;
if one uses Jié to deceive Yáo,
it's like throwing an egg against a stone,
or stirring boiling water with a finger,
or having a feather tread on raging fire,
entering, it will be burned up.
How then can it be deceived?
Therefore, the army of a benevolent person,
when drawn, is like the sharp blade of Mòyé,
whoever encounters it is cut;
when sharp, it's like the keen edge of Mòyé,
Those who oppose them collapse.
They are stationed in a circular formation but halt in a square formation,
like a flat rock.
Those who attack them only stumble and retreat;
how can they be deceived?
Therefore, the army of a benevolent ruler, if led by a general,
all three armies work together with a common strength,
and those above and below are of one mind.
The relationship of a minister to his ruler,
and of those below to those above,
is like that of a son serving his father,
like that of a younger brother serving his elder brother,
like hands and feet defending the head and eyes and covering the chest and abdomen.
To deceive and attack them,
is the same as alarming them first and then attacking them later;
it is the same thing.
How can they be deceived?
Moreover, a violent and chaotic ruler,
with whom will he reach the goal?
Those with whom he reaches the goal,
must be his people.
The people are intimate with me and rejoice like they do with their parents;
they like me and are fragrant like pepper and orchids.
Looking back at their ruler,
they view him like a branding,
like an enemy.
Even if people have the character of Jié Zhí,
how could there be anyone willing to do what they hate and harm what they love?
It is like making one's grandsons and great-grandsons kill their own parents.
The *Shī* says:
“Wǔ Wáng raised his banner,
reverently grasping his battle-axe,
like a blazing fire,
then none would dare to oppose us."
This is what it means.”
Xiào Chéng Wáng and Lín Wǔ Jūn said:
“Good!
May we ask about the army of a true king?”
Sūn Qīng said:
“The generals and commanders are
a minor matter.
Let me list the affairs of a true king
and the methods of a ruler.”
In the past, Qín and Wèi were allied states.
Qí and Chǔ made an agreement and intended to attack Wèi.
Wèi sent men to seek aid from Qín.
The carriages and canopies [of envoys] were within sight of each other,
but Qín did not send out aid.
Among the people of Wèi there was one Táng Qiě,
over ninety years old,

If they do not agree, even flesh and blood will become enemies,
such as Zhū, Xiàng, Guǎn, and Cài.
If the present rulers can employ the perspicacity of Qi and Qin,
and listen like Song and Lu,
then the Five Hegemons would not be worth comparing,
and the Three Kings would be easy to match.
Therefore, the sage kings were enlightened,
abandoning the heart of Zi,
and were able to not be pleased by the worthiness of Tián Cháng;
enfeoffed the descendants of Bǐ Gān,
repaired the graves of pregnant women,
thus their accomplishments covered the world,
why?
Because their desire for goodness had no limit.
Jìn Wén Gōng befriended his enemy,
and became a strong hegemon among the feudal lords;
Qí Huán Gōng employed his enemy,
and rectified the world in one stroke,
why?
Because kindness and diligence,
were sincerely added to the heart,
and cannot be borrowed with empty words.
As for Qin employing the laws of Shāng Yāng,
weakening Han and Wei to the east,
establishing strength over the world,
and in the end, tearing Shāng Jūn apart by chariots;
Yue employing the strategies of Dàfū Zhǒng,
capturing the strong Wu,
To dominate the Central Kingdom [China],
ultimately leads to one's own execution.
Therefore, Sūn Shū'áo resigned from the position of prime minister three times without regret,
and Yúlíng Zhòngzǐ resigned from the position of the Three Dukes,
to irrigate gardens for others.
If the rulers of today could truly cast aside their arrogance,
and cherish the intention of rewarding others,
reveal their innermost thoughts,
show their true feelings,
lay bare their hearts,
bestow generous kindness,
share weal and woe with them,
and remain unchanged towards scholars,
then even Jié's dog
could be made to bark at Yáo;
Zhí's guest
could be made to assassinate Yóu,
how much more so when relying on the power of a ten-thousand-chariot kingdom,
and borrowing the resources of a sage king?
In that case, Jīng Kē, who brought ruin upon seven clans,
and Yào Lí, who burned his wife and children,
are surely not sufficient to be considered the way of a great king!
The pearls of bright moons,
the jades that glow in the night,
if used to throw at people in the darkness of the road,
there is no one who would not grip their swords and glare at each other.
Why?
Because there is no means of introduction.
The roots of a gnarled tree,
twisted and strange,
that become the supports of a chariot for ten thousand,
are first given form by those on the left and right.
Therefore, without prior recommendation,
even if one presents the pearl of Marquis Suí,
or the jade of nocturnal radiance,
it will only be enough to incur resentment and not be appreciated.
Therefore, if someone introduces you first,
then even with withered wood and rotten stumps,
they establish merit and are not forgotten.
Now, let commoners and impoverished scholars across the land,
even though they possess the skills of Yáo and Shùn,
and the eloquence of Yī and Guǎn,
inherently lack the appearance of having a background,
and desire to exhaust their spirit,
reveal their loyalty and sincerity,
and assist the ruler in governing,
the ruler will certainly adopt the habit of pressing his sword and glancing sidelong at them.
This is to say that commoners are not allowed to assume the role of withered wood and rotten stumps.
Therefore, wise kings regulate the world and control customs,
transforming things alone on the potter's wheel,
able to not be swayed by lowly and chaotic words,
and not be deceived by the mouths of the multitude.
Therefore, the Qin Emperor trusted the words of the Palace Attendant Méng Tián,
and believed the rhetoric of Jīng Kē,
hence the dagger was stealthily drawn.
King Wén of Zhōu hunted in the Jīng and Wèi Rivers,
He carried Lǚ Shàng back with him,
and thus became king of the world.
Qín trusted those around him and was murdered,
Zhōu employed a diverse group of people and became king.
Why is this?
It is because they could transcend the words of the narrow-minded,
embrace opinions from beyond their borders,
and observe the broad and enlightened path alone.
Now, rulers are沉溺drowned in flattering words,
constrained by the restrictions of their inner chambers,
causing unrestrained talents
to be treated the same as ordinary oxen and horses.
This is why Bào Jiāo was resentful of the world and did not remain to enjoy the pleasures of wealth and status.
I have heard that those who adorn themselves grandly for court
do not use private matters to enact righteousness;
those who cultivate a noble reputation
do not harm their conduct for personal gain.
Therefore, because the village was named "Victorious Mother,"
Zēngzǐ did not enter;
because the city was named "Chāogē,"
Mòzǐ turned his carriage around.
Now, if you cause broad-minded scholars of the world
to be caged by the power of majesty,
threatened by the nobility of position,
to turn their faces and soil their conduct,
in order to serve flattering people,
and seek closeness with those around them,
then the king will only have those who lie dead, dwell in caves and dens, and live in the mountains,
How could there be someone who exhausts their spirit to rush to the palace gate!"
He wrote to King Xiào of Qín,
and King Xiào immediately appointed him,
and he eventually became an honored guest.

Guǎn Zhòng said to Duke Huán of Qí:
"As for cultivating fields and establishing settlements,
opening up land and planting grains,

I request that he be appointed as the Officer of Agriculture.
As for ascending and descending, bowing and yielding,
advancing and retreating with practiced ease,
I am not as good as Xí Péng.
I request that he be appointed as the Grand Herald.
As for entering early and leaving late,
offending the ruler's countenance,
offering loyal remonstrations,
not valuing wealth and status,
not avoiding death,
then I am not as good as Dōngguō Yá.
I request that he be appointed as a remonstrating minister.
As for deciding lawsuits fairly,
not falsely accusing the innocent,
not killing the guiltless,
then I am not as good as Xián Níng.
I request that he be appointed as the Grand Judge.
On broad plains and in vast parks,
where carts do not get their axles entangled,
and soldiers do not turn on their heels,
when the drums are beaten and the soldiers of the three armies
view death as returning home,
Then I am not as good as Wángzǐ Chéngfǔ,
Please appoint him as Grand Marshal.
If you, my lord, wish to govern the country and strengthen the military,
Then these five men are sufficient;
If you wish to become a Hegemon-King,
Then Yí Wú is here."

Duke Huán could employ the worthy,

the second time you tell Zhòngfǔ,

"Before I obtained Zhòngfǔ, it was difficult;
now that I have obtained Zhòngfǔ,

Therefore, a true king labors in seeking men,
and is at ease in having obtained worthy men.
Shùn promoted many worthy men to positions,
let his robes hang down,
and governed the world by being respectful and doing nothing.
Tāng and Wén used Yī and Lǚ,
Chéng Wáng used Zhōu and Shào,
and punishments were put aside and not used,
weapons were put down and not moved.
This was because they used many worthy men.
Huán Gōng's use of Guǎn Zhòng was on a smaller scale.
Therefore, he reached the point of hegemony but could not achieve kingship.
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ said:
"How small was Guǎn Zhòng's capacity!"
He probably admired his meeting Huán Gōng,
but regretted that he could not achieve kingship.
The most enlightened rulers are not like this;
Suǒ yòng dà yǐ. [What is employed] is truly great.

Cǐ zhī wèi yě. [This is what it means.]

Wèi Wénhóu's younger brother was named Jì Chénɡ,
his friend was named Dí Huánɡ.
Wénhóu wanted to appoint one of them as prime minister but could not decide,

Kè replied,
"If you, my lord, are choosing a prime minister,

Wénhóu said,
"Good!"
Because Wánɡsūn ɡǒu Duān was deemed unworthy, Dí Huánɡ recommended him;
because Yuè Shānɡ was virtuous,
Jì Chénɡ recommended him,
therefore, Jì Chénɡ was appointed prime minister.
Therefore, to know people is wisdom,
to advance the worthy receives the highest reward.
Jì Chénɡ, because of his knowing virtue,
Wénhóu made him prime minister.
Jì Chénɡ and Dí Huánɡ
were both close ministers and relatives;
based on who they recommended, which was virtuous, they were distinguished.
Therefore, the words of Lǐ Kè are correct.
Lord Mèngcháng asked Bái Guī, saying:
"The reputation of Marquis Wén of Wèi exceeds that of Duke Huán,

Bái Guī replied:
"Marquis Wén of Wèi took Zǐxià as his teacher,
befriended Tián Zǐfāng,

this is why his reputation exceeds that of Duke Huán.
When seeking a prime minister, he said:
'Which is acceptable, Chéng or Huáng?'
This is why his achievements do not match the Five Hegemons.
Using personal affection to obstruct public appointment,
those in office are unequal to their tasks,

However, the reason why his name and reputation are eminent and glorious
is because of the support of these three gentlemen.
If he had made these three gentlemen prime ministers,
then the achievements of a king would have been realized,

Shī Kuàng was in attendance

Bīn Xū Wú is good at harmonizing and blending them.
The soup is already cooked;
it is presented and offered.
But if the ruler does not eat it,
who can force him?
It is also the power of the ruler."

The grand officer Cáo Guì of Lǔ said to Duke Zhuāng,

Thus, the lord did not betray his word.
Cáo Guì was worthy of revenge,

Consequently, he did not betray.
The lords of the world all readily returned to him.
He held the meeting at Juàn,
and the alliance at Yōu.
The lords all attended.
He held the meeting at Yánggǔ,
and the alliance at Guànzé.
Even distant states came.
He campaigned south against the powerful state of Chǔ,

He campaigned north against the Shān Róng,

He preserved three perished states,

He honored and served the House of Zhōu,

The origin of his trustworthiness began with the alliance at Kē.
Duke Wén of Jìn attacked Yuán.
He agreed with his officers to wait five days.
After five days, Yuán had not surrendered.
Duke Wén ordered them to leave.
An officer said:
"Yuán will surrender in no more than three days,

The Lord said:
"To gain Yuan and lose trust,
I will not do it."
The people of Yuan heard this and said:
"Their lord is so righteous,
we cannot but surrender."
So they surrendered.
The people of Wen heard this,
and also requested to surrender.
Therefore, it is said:
"By attacking Yuan, Wen surrendered,"
this is what it means.
Thereupon,
the lords of the feudal states submitted to him,

held the meeting at Jiantu and the alliance at Wen,
later, he defeated the powerful Chu in the south,
and respected the Zhou royal house,

This was fundamentally due to his trustworthiness when he attacked Yuan.
