Before the encirclement was complete, ten sections of the city wall collapsed on their own.

He allowed them to rebuild the wall and then attacked.
Zhōngmù, hearing of his righteousness,

Soon after, the Jìn 晉 people, who had come to rescue Zhèng 鄭, arrived,

Zhuāng Wáng 莊王 permitted it.

strong state;

Zhuāng Wáng 莊王 said:

Thereupon, he turned the army around to meet the Jìn 晉 invaders.
Zhuāng Wáng 莊王 took up the drumstick and beat the drum,

The Jìn 晉 people came,
crossed the river southwards;
and when they were defeated and fled in disarray,

In the end, they fought over the boats and struck the oars with blades,

Zhuāng Wáng 莊王 said:
"Alas!
The inability of our two lords to get along,

Thereupon he withdrew his troops to let the Jìn invaders pass.
The *Shī* says,
"The gentle he does not devour,
the strong he does not spit out,
he does not insult widowers and widows,
he does not fear the powerful and oppressive."
This describes Zhuāng Wáng.
The people of Jìn attacked Chǔ,
retreating three *shè* (a military unit of distance) did not stop them.
A high official said,
"Please allow us to attack them."
Zhuāng Wáng said,
"In the time of the former lord,
Jìn did not attack Chǔ;
now that it has reached my reign,

The high official said,

Jìn attacks Chǔ;
this is my fault.

King Zhuāng bowed down weeping and arose,

this is what is meant by 'those above and those below are of one mind,'

They cannot be attacked."
Therefore, that night they returned their army.
Kǒngzǐ heard of this and said:
"King Zhuāng of Chǔ achieved hegemony;
he had a method for it.
A low-ranking officer with a single word caused the enemy to retreat,
thereby securing the state,
his hegemony,
is it not fitting?"
The "Book of Poetry" says:
"Cherish those far away and be able to treat kindly those near,
thereby stabilizing our king."
This is what it refers to.
Duke Wén of Jìn was about to attack Yè.
Zhào Shuāi spoke of the way to conquer Yè.
Duke Wén used it and conquered Yè.
He was about to reward Zhào Shuāi.
Zhào Shuāi said:
"Will Your Lordship reward the branch?
Or reward the root?
If you reward the branch,
then the riders and charioteers will remain;
if you reward the root,
then your servant has heard it from Xì Hǔ."
The Duke summoned Xì Hǔ and said:
"Shuāi spoke of the way to conquer Yè,
and then it was conquered.
I am about to reward him,
but he said:
'I have heard it from you, sir,
you should be rewarded.'"
Xì Hǔ replied:
"To speak is easy,
to act is difficult;
your servant is merely the one who spoke."
The Duke said:
"Sir, do not decline."
Xì Hǔ dared not firmly decline,
and then received the reward.
4.13 There was a grand master of Liáng named Sòng Jiù,
once served as the magistrate of a border county,
bordering Chu.
The border posts of Liang and the border posts of Chu both grew melons,
each having a certain number.
The people of the Liang border post diligently and frequently watered their melons,
Liáng dàfū yǒu Sòng Jiù zhě,
and the melons were beautiful.
The people of Chu were lazy and rarely watered their melons,
and the melons were bad.
The Chu magistrate, because of the beauty of the Liang melons, was angry at the badness of his post's melons.
The hearts of the Chu post people resented the superiority of the Liang post,
so they went at night and secretly scratched the Liang post's melons,
causing them all to die and wither.
The Liang post discovered this,
and requested permission from their commandant
to secretly go and retaliate by scratching the Chu post's melons.
The commandant asked Sòng Jiù about this.
Jiù said:
"How terrible!
How can this be done?
It is the path to resentment and disaster.
To return evil for evil,
how narrow-minded is that!
If I were to instruct you,
I would certainly order people to go every evening
to secretly and kindly water the Chu post's melons at night,
without letting them know."
Therefore,
Liáng Tíng 梁亭 then every evening secretly watered the melons of the Chǔ 楚 pavilion.
The Chǔ 楚 pavilion man, in the morning, went to inspect the melons,
and they were all watered again.
The melons became more beautiful day by day.
The Chǔ 楚 pavilion man was surprised and investigated,
and it was discovered to be the Liáng 梁 pavilion man.
The Chǔ 楚 magistrate heard of it,
was greatly pleased,
and therefore reported everything to the King of Chǔ 楚.
The King of Chǔ 楚 heard of it,
felt grieved and ashamed,
feeling self-pity in his heart.
He told his officials,
"Those who are harvesting melons, should they not have other crimes?"
"This is the hidden kindness of Liáng 梁."
Therefore, he apologized with heavy gifts,
and requested to establish diplomatic relations with the King of Liáng 梁.
The King of Chǔ 楚 then regularly praised and wished good fortune to the King of Liáng 梁 to show his sincerity.
Therefore, the friendship between Liáng 梁 and Chǔ 楚,
began from this incident in Sòng 宋.
A saying goes,
"Turn defeat into success,
turn misfortune into blessing."
Lǎozǐ 老子 said,
"Repay hatred with virtue."
This is what it means.
If a person is not virtuous,
how can he be effective?
The state of Liang once had a doubtful criminal case.
Half of the court officials thought the accused should be punished,
and half thought he should be acquitted.
Even King Liang was uncertain.
King Liang said:
"Zhū Gōng of Tao,
who became as wealthy as a state leader while being a commoner,
must have extraordinary wisdom."
Therefore, he summoned Zhū Gōng and asked him:
"Liang has a doubtful criminal case.
Half of the prison officials think the accused should be punished,
and half think he should not be punished.
Even I am uncertain.
I want you to decide this,
what should be done?"
Zhū Gōng said:
"Your servant,
a humble commoner,
does not know how to judge criminal cases.
However,
my family has two white jade disks.
Their colors are similar,
their diameters are similar,
their luster is similar,
yet one is worth a thousand gold pieces,
and the other is worth five hundred gold pieces."
The King said:
"Their diameters and luster are similar,
one costs a thousand gold,
the other costs five hundred gold,
why is that?"
Zhū Gōng said:
"View them from the side,
one is twice as thick,
therefore it costs a thousand gold."
King of Liáng said:
"Good!"
Therefore, when there is doubt in a trial, one should err on the side of acquittal;
when there is doubt in a reward, one should err on the side of giving it.
The state of Liáng was greatly pleased.
From this, we can see that
a thin wall will quickly collapse,
thin silk will quickly tear,
thin vessels will quickly break,
thin wine will quickly turn sour,
and things that are thin that can last a long time
probably do not exist.
Therefore, those who possess a state, nurture the people, and administer governance and education,
should be generous with them, that is all.
King Huì of Chǔ ate cold pickled vegetables and found a leech,
and then swallowed it.
His stomach became ill and he could not eat.
Lìngyǐn (令尹) entered and asked,
"How did the king contract this illness?"
The king said,
"I ate cold pickled vegetables and ingested leeches.
If I considered blaming those responsible but did not carry out their punishment,
then the law would be abandoned and authority not established.
This is not the way to make the state renowned.
If I were to blame them and carry out the execution,
then the cooks and food supervisors
would all, according to the law, deserve to die,
but my heart cannot bear it.
Therefore, I was afraid of the leeches being discovered,
and so I swallowed them."
Lìngyǐn (令尹) avoided his seat, bowed twice, and congratulated him, saying,
"I have heard that Heaven has no favorites,
but only aids those with virtue.
Your Majesty has benevolent virtue,
and is supported by Heaven,
so the illness will not be harmful."
That night,
the leeches that were in King Huì (惠王) passed out,
and the chronic heart and stomach ailments were all cured.
The seeing and hearing of Heaven
must not be neglected.
The people of Zhèng (鄭) were gathering at the village school,
to discuss the merits and demerits of the government.
Rán Míng said to Zǐchǎn,
"Why not destroy the village schools?"
Zǐchǎn said,
"Why do that?
The people go there morning and evening
to discuss the merits and demerits of the government's policies.
What they deem good,
I will implement;
what they deem bad,
I will change.
They are my teachers.
How could I destroy them?
I have heard that in governing a state,
one should use loyalty and trustworthiness to diminish resentment,
and not use force to prevent resentment.
It is like damming a river:
when a major breach occurs,
it will inevitably harm many people,
and I will not be able to save them.
It is better to make small openings to guide the flow,
and I will hear their complaints and remedy them."
Rán Míng said,
"I, Rán,
now know that you, sir, are truly trustworthy and worth serving.
I am truly untalented.
If you truly implement this,
then the state of Zhèng will truly rely on it.
It will not only benefit a few ministers like us."
Confucius,
upon hearing these words,
said:
"Judging from this,
people say that Zǐchǎn is unkind,
I do not believe it."
Duke Huán drank wine with Guǎn Zhòng, Bào Shū, and Níng Qī.
Duke Huán said to Bào Shū:
"Please offer a toast for me!"
Bào Shū held up his wine cup and rose, saying:
"I toast my lord,
may you not forget when you fled and were in Jǔ;
may Guǎn Zhòng not forget when he was bound and followed from Lǔ;
may Níng Zǐ not forget when he fed oxen beneath the cart."
Duke Huán moved from his mat and bowed twice, saying:
"I and these two great officers,
will all not forget your words,
the altars of the state of Qí,
will certainly not be abandoned."
This speaks of always remembering times of hardship,
and certainly not becoming arrogant.
Duke Huán hunted,
and arrived at Màiqiū,
and saw a villager from Màiqiū,
and asked him:
"What do you do?"
He replied:
"I am a person from the town of Màiqiū."
The Duke said:
"How old are you?"
He replied:
"I am eighty-three years old."
The Duke said:
"How wonderful is your longevity!
Use your longevity to wish me well."
The person from the town of Màiqiū said:
"I wish for my lord,
that my lord may have great longevity,
and that he may consider gold and jade as cheap, and people as treasures."
Duke Huán said:
"Excellent!
Supreme virtue is never solitary,
and good words must be repeated.
Sir, please repeat it."
The person from the town of Màiqiū said:
"I wish for my lord,
that my lord may not be ashamed to learn,
nor dislike asking those beneath him,
that wise men may be at his side,
and that he may gain people who will remonstrate."
Duke Huán said:
"Excellent!
Supreme virtue is never solitary,
"Good words must be said three times;
My son, you have only said one."
A man from the town of Màiqiū 麥丘 said:
"I wish that the lord
would not offend his ministers and the common people."
Duke Huán 桓公 was displeased and changed countenance, saying:
"I have heard that
a son can offend his father,
and a minister can offend his lord,
but I have never heard of a lord offending his ministers.
This one statement
is not a match for the other two.
Change it."
The man from the town of Màiqiū 麥丘 sat down, bowed, and rose, saying:
"This one statement
is superior to the other two.
If a son offends his father,
it can be resolved through aunts, sisters, and uncles,
and the father can forgive him.
If a minister offends his lord,
it can be apologized for through favorites and attendants,
and the lord can forgive him.
In the past, Jié 桀 offended Tāng 湯,
and Zhòu 紂 offended King Wǔ 武王.
These are cases of lords offending their ministers,
but there was no one to apologize for them,
and they have not been forgiven to this day."
The Duke said:
"Shàn!
It is thanks to the blessings of the state,
and the spirits of the altars of soil and grain,
that I, your ruler, have obtained you, my son, here."
He helped him up and put him in the carriage,
personally drove him home,
treated him with ceremony at court,
enfeoffed him with Maiqiu and entrusted him with the administration of government there.
4.19 Duke Ai asked Confucius, saying:
"I, your ruler, was born in the depths of the palace,
and grew up in the hands of women.
I, your ruler, have never known grief,
have never known sorrow,
have never known toil,
have never known fear,
have never known danger."
Confucius moved aside from his mat and said:
"The question of my lord,
is indeed the question of a sagely ruler.
I, Qiu,
am a petty man,
how can I be sufficient to speak of it?"
Duke Ai said:
"No,
please take your seat,
without you,
wú suǒ wén zhī yǐ!"
Kǒngzǐ took his seat and said:
"Indeed.
When the ruler enters the temple gate,
ascends from the eastern steps,
looks up and sees the rafters and beams,
looks down and sees the low tables and mats,
the implements remain,
but the people are gone.
If the ruler reflects on this with sorrow,
then what sorrow will not come?
If the ruler dresses and puts on his cap before dawn,
and listens to court at daybreak,
and one matter is not answered,
it is the beginning of chaos.
If the ruler reflects on this with worry,
then what worry will not come?
If the ruler listens to court at daybreak,
and retires when the sun slants westward,
and among the descendants of the feudal lords,
there are surely those who are at the ruler's court,
if the ruler reflects on this with toil,
then what toil will not come?
If the ruler goes out through the four gates of Lǔ,
to gaze upon the four outskirts of Lǔ,
the ruins of destroyed states,
arranged, surely there are a number of them.
If the ruler reflects on this with fear,
then what fear will not come?
Qiū has heard it said,
the ruler is a boat,
the common people are water,
water can carry the boat,
water can overturn the boat.
If the ruler uses this to consider danger,
then what danger will *not* arrive?
To grasp the handle of the state,
to tread above the people,
is to be apprehensive, like using rotten rope to control a runaway horse.
The *Book of Changes* says:
"Treading on the tiger's tail."
The *Book of Odes* says:
"As if treading on thin ice."
Is it not dangerous!"
Duke Āi bowed twice and said:
"Although I am not clever,
I beg to attend to these words."
and saw the ruins of the old city of the destroyed state of the Guō clan,
and asked a rustic:
"What are these ruins?"
The rustic said:
"These are the ruins of the Guō clan."
Duke Huán said:
"Why did the Guō clan become ruins?"
The rustic said:
"The Guō clan esteemed the good and detested the bad."
Duke Huán said:
"Esteeming the good and detesting the bad
is a good deed for people,
Why then is their land desolate?"
The commoner said:
"Praising good but unable to implement it,
hating evil but unable to eliminate it,
is why their land is desolate."
Duke Huán returned
and told Guǎn Zhòng about it.
He asked:
"Who was that man?"
Duke Huán said:
"I don't know."
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"You, my lord, are also just like a Guō Shì."
Thereupon,
Duke Huán summoned the commoner and rewarded him.
Duke Wén of Jìn was hunting in Guó.
He met an old man and asked him:
"Guó has been Guó for a long time,
and you have lived here for a long time.
Guó fell.
"Could there be a reason for this?"
He replied:
"The Lord of Guo, when he should decide, is unable to do so;
when he should advise, there is no one to do it with him.
Unable to decide,
and furthermore, unable to employ people,
In the past, Duke Huán of Qí went on an excursion in the countryside,
this is the reason why Guo perished."
Duke Wén ceased his hunting and returned,
he met Zhào Shuāi and told him about it.
Zhào Shuāi said:
"Where is that person now?"
The Duke said:
"I did not bring him back with me."
Zhào Shuāi said:
"The gentlemen of old,
listened to their words and employed their persons;
the gentlemen of today,
listen to their words and discard their persons.
Alas!
It is a cause for concern for the state of Jìn."
Duke Wén then summoned him and rewarded him.
Thereupon,
the state of Jìn delighted in accepting good advice,
and Duke Wén eventually achieved hegemony as a result.
Duke Píng of Jìn passed by Jiǔyuán and sighed, saying:
"Alas!
This land nurtures many of my good ministers!
If the dead could be brought back to life,
to whom would I return?"
Shū Xiàng replied,
"Perhaps Zhào Wǔ!"
Duke Píng said,
"You are biased towards your teacher."
He replied,
"Your servant dares to speak of Zhào Wǔ's character.
Standing, he appears unable to bear the weight of his clothes;
speaking, it seems his words barely escape his mouth.
Yet, he personally recommended forty-six men from humble backgrounds,
all of whom understood his intentions,
and the state heavily relied on them.
When Wén Zǐ died,
all forty-six men took their places as guests,
showing he had no private favors to grant.
Therefore, I believe he is worthy."
Duke Píng said,
"Good."
Indeed, Zhào Wǔ was a worthy minister,
serving as chancellor of Jìn,
and there were no wars in the realm for nine years.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* says,
"It was due to the strength of Jìn's Zhào Wǔ
that he was able to fully obtain men's service."
Yè Gōng Zhūliáng asked Yuè Wáng Fù:
"What kind of person is the Jìn grandee, Zhào Wénzǐ?"
He replied:
"He loves learning and accepts advice."
Yè Gōng said:
"I suspect that is not the whole picture."
He replied:
"Loving learning
is wisdom;
accepting advice
is benevolence.
The [Yangtze] River emerges from Wènshān Mountain,
its source like the mouth of a jar,
and when it reaches the state of Chǔ,
it is ten *lǐ* wide.
There is no other reason for this
than that its downstream tributaries are numerous.
If a person loves learning and accepts advice,
it is fitting that he will be established.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'Only a wise man
will be told wise words,
and follow the path of virtue.'
This is what it means."
Zhōng Zǐqī heard someone playing the *qìng* chime at night and felt sorrow.
At dawn, he summoned the person and asked:
“What is the reason?
That you strike the chime-stone with such sorrow?"
He replied,
“My father killed a man and was not apprehended.
My mother was apprehended and became a slave of the state.
I was apprehended and became a chime-stone player for the state.
I have not seen my mother
for three years now.
Yesterday, at the market by the lodging, I saw her.
I wanted to redeem her, but I have no money.
And my body is also possessed by the state.
That is why I am sorrowful.”
Zhōng Zǐqī said,
“The sorrow is in your heart,
not in your hands,
nor in the wood or stone.
Sorrow in the heart, and wood and stone respond to it,
is due to utmost sincerity.
If a ruler can only move from within with utmost sincerity,
the myriad people will surely respond and be moved.
The sincerity of Yáo and Shùn
moved the myriad kingdoms
and moved heaven and earth.
Therefore, even those in remote lands followed the wind,
and phoenixes and unicorns soared and danced.
Down to the smallest creatures,
all found their proper place.
The *Yì* says,
"In Zhong Fu, even pigs and fish bring good fortune."
This is what it means.
A brave warrior shouts once,
and the entire army gives way.
This is the sincerity of a soldier.
In the past, Xióng Qú of Chǔ was walking at night,
and saw a sleeping stone.
He thought it was a crouching tiger.
He drew his bow and shot at it,
burying the arrow and its feathers.
He looked down,
and knew it was a stone.
He turned back and shot at it again,
but the arrow shattered without leaving a mark.
Xióng Qú saw his own sincerity,
and metal and stone were opened by it.
How much more so, people's hearts?
If one sings but others do not harmonize,
if one acts but others do not follow,
there must be something incomplete within.
To rectify the world without leaving one's mat,
one must seek it within oneself.
Confucius said:
"If one's self is upright,
orders are followed without being issued;
if one's self is not upright,
Even if he issues orders, they will not be followed."
The reason why the former kings, with their respectful bows and gestures, caused the four seas to pay them homage,
was truly because their virtue was supreme,
and it had already manifested outwardly.
Therefore, the *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
"The king was truly sincere,"
"and Xú Fāng subsequently came."
This is what it means.
In Qí, there was a comet.
The Marquis of Qí ordered the *zhù* (prayer official) to perform a ritual to avert it.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"It will be of no benefit;
it will only bring about deception.
The Way of Heaven does not flatter,
nor does it change its decrees.
How can one avert it with rituals?
Moreover, the presence of a comet in the sky
is to remove impurities.
If the ruler has no impure virtue,
then what is there to avert?
If the virtue *is* impure,
how would averting it diminish it?
The *Shī* says:
'Oh, this King Wén,
cautious and respectful,
clearly served the High God,
To continually cherish much good fortune,
their virtue does not turn away,
and so they receive the states.
If the ruler does not violate virtue,
the states will come,
why worry about a comet?
The *Odes* says:
"I have nothing to oversee,
the Xia sovereign and the Shang,
used disorder as a cause,
and the people ultimately drifted and perished."
If virtue turns to disorder,
the people will drift and perish,
the actions of the prayer scribes,
will be unable to remedy it."
The duke was pleased,
and then stopped.
During the time of Duke Jǐng of Sòng,
Mars was in the constellation Heart,
he was afraid,
and summoned Zǐ Wéi and asked,
"Mars is in the Heart,
what does this mean?"
Zǐ Wéi said:
"Mars,
is heavenly punishment;
"The heart,
in the astrological divisions of Sòng,
indicates disaster befalling the ruler."
"However,"
Zǐ Wéi said, "it can be transferred to the prime minister."
The Duke said,
"The prime minister
is the one I employ to govern the state,
and to transfer death to him
is inauspicious.
I, the lonely one, will bear it myself."
Zǐ Wéi said,
"It can be transferred to the people."
The Duke said,
"If the people die,
whom shall I rule?
I would rather die alone."
Zǐ Wéi said,
"It can be transferred to the harvest."
The Duke said,
"If the harvest fails,
the people will starve and surely die.
To be a ruler
and wish to kill his people in order to save himself,
who would consider me their ruler?
It is clear that my life is indeed at its end.
Speak no more about it."
Zǐ Wéi turned back and walked away,
faced north and bowed twice,
and said,
"Your servant dares to congratulate you, my lord!
Heaven dwells high and listens to the humble.
You, my lord, have spoken three times with the words of a benevolent man,
Heaven will surely reward you three times.
Tonight, the stars will surely move their positions,
and you, my lord, will have your life extended by twenty-one years."
The duke said:
"How do you know this?"
He replied:
"You, my lord, have three acts of goodness,
therefore, three rewards.
The stars will surely shift three times,
shifting seven stars each time.
Each star represents one year.
Three times seven is twenty-one,
therefore it is said your life will be extended by twenty-one years.
Your servant requests to lie prostrate before Your Majesty to observe it.
If the stars do not move,
your servant begs to die for it."
The duke said:
"Alright."
That night,
the stars shifted their positions three times,
as Zǐ Wéi had said.
Lǎozǐ said:
"He who can bear the misfortunes of a state,
This is what it means to be the king of the world."
During the time of King Kāng of Sòng,
a sparrowhawk gave birth to a magpie in the corner of the city.
He had a historian divine it, saying:
"Something small gives birth to something large,
it will certainly dominate the world."
King Kāng was greatly pleased.
Thereupon he destroyed Téng and attacked Xuē,
taking the land north of the Huái River.
He became even more self-confident,
desiring his hegemony to be quickly achieved.
Therefore, he shot at the sky and whipped the ground,
beheaded the altars of the soil and grain, and burned them, saying:
"My majesty subdues heaven, earth, ghosts, and spirits."
He cursed the elder statesmen who advised him as headless coffins,
to show his bravery.
He cut open the backs of hunchbacks,
and chopped off the shins of those who waded through the morning dew,
and the people of the state were greatly terrified.
Qí heard of this and attacked him,
the people scattered,
the city could not be defended,
and the king fled to the guesthouse of the Marquis of Ér,
where he contracted an illness and died.
Therefore, seeing an auspicious sign and acting improperly,
the auspicious sign turns into disaster.
Your servant Xiàng deduces it using the "Commentary on the Great Plan."
The divination of the Sòng historians is wrong.
This is a black omen,
what the commentary calls a "black defect."
It is like the black omen of the starling in Lǔ.
It belongs to the category of not planning for the consequences of haste.
The sparrowhawk is black,
it eats sparrows,
is larger than sparrows,
and harms sparrows.
It is something that seizes and strikes,
a greedy kind.
For a sparrow to give birth to a sparrowhawk
means that the ruler of Sòng will engage in hasty, violent attacks and greedy actions,
rejecting remonstrance and bringing about great disaster to harm himself.
Therefore, a sparrow giving birth to a sparrowhawk in the corner of the city
signifies the destruction of the state;
it clearly foretells disaster and harm to the state.
Kāng Wáng did not realize this,
and consequently perished.
This is its effect.

Zǐxià said,

I will only take those who defy my command."
The states south of the Hàn River heard of this,
and said:
"The virtue of Tāng has extended even to birds and beasts!"
Forty states submitted to him.
If people set nets on all four sides,
they might not catch a bird.
Tāng removed three sides,
and set a net on only one side,
using it to ensnare forty states.
He did not merely ensnare birds.
King Wén of Zhōu built the Spirit Terrace,
and also created ponds.
Excavating the ground,
they found the bones of a dead person.
The officer reported this to King Wén.
King Wén said:
"Rebury them."
The officer said:
"These have no owner."
King Wén said:
"He who possesses the empire
is the lord of the empire;
he who possesses a state
Is the ruler of a state.
Guǎrén (寡人, "I," a term used by rulers) is indeed its ruler,
so why seek another ruler?"
Thereupon, he ordered officials to use robes and a coffin to rebury him.
The world heard of this,
and all said,
"Wén Wáng (文王) is wise indeed!
His beneficence extends even to decayed bones;
how much more so to living people?"
Some acquire treasures and endanger their states,
but Wén Wáng (文王) acquired decayed bones to convey his intentions,
and the world's hearts turned to him.
Guǎn Zhòng (管仲) tutored Qí (齊) prince Gōngzǐ Jiū (公子紏),
and Bào Shū (鮑叔) tutored prince Gōngzǐ Xiǎobái (公子小白).
Qí (齊) duke's grandson Wúzhī (無知) killed Duke Xiāng (襄公).
Gōngzǐ Jiū (公子糾) fled to Lǔ (魯),
and Xiǎobái (小白) fled to Jǔ (莒).
The people of Qí (齊) executed Wúzhī (無知),
and welcomed Gōngzǐ Jiū (公子糾) from Lǔ (魯).
Gōngzǐ Jiū (公子糾) and Xiǎobái (小白) vied to enter (Qí).
Guǎn Zhòng (管仲) shot Xiǎobái (小白),
hitting his belt hook.
Xiǎobái (小白) feigned death,
and consequently entered first.
He became known as Duke Huán of Qí (齊桓公).
Gōngzǐ Jiū (公子糾) died,
Guǎn Zhòng fled to Lǔ.
Duke Huán came to power,
the state stabilized,
and he sent men to welcome Guǎn Zhòng from Lǔ,
then established him as Zhòngfǔ (Second Father),
entrusting the state to him and listening to him.
He united the feudal lords nine times,
rectified the world once,
and became the leader of the Five Hegemons.
Lǐ Fúxū was
the one in charge of the residence of the Jìn prince, Chóng'ěr.
When Prince Chóng'ěr fled from Jìn,
Lǐ Fúxū stole his valuables and fled.
Prince Chóng'ěr returned to his state,
and was established as ruler.
Lǐ Fúxū arrived at the gate wishing to see him.
Duke Wén was in the middle of bathing,
and his attendant reported this.
Duke Wén, holding his hair, replied,
"Is it my Fúxū?"
He said,
"Yes."
He said to Fúxū,
"Do you still have the face to see me again?"
The attendant told Lǐ Fúxū this.
Fúxū replied,
"Your servant has heard it said that
one who washes their hair has a clouded mind,
and one with a clouded mind speaks perversely.
Does Your Lordship have a clouded mind?
Why are you being so perverse?"
The messenger reported back,
and Wén Gōng saw him and said,
"If you stole my treasures and fled,
I would think you would have no face to see me.
You say, 'Why is Your Lordship being so perverse?'
What is the meaning of this?"
Fú Xū said,
"Indeed,
when Your Lordship returned to the state,
half of the state was uneasy.
Would Your Lordship rather abandon half the state?
Would there then be a complete Jìn?"
Wén Gōng said,
"What do you mean?"
Fú Xū said,
"None have offended Your Lordship more than Fú Xū.
Your Lordship said you would pardon Fú Xū
and prominently appoint him as your right-hand man.
If a crime as serious as Fú Xū's
is forgiven by Your Lordship,
how much more so those whose offenses are lighter than Fú Xū's?"
Wén Gōng said,
"I understand your meaning."
「Wén mìng yǐ.」 "I have heard your order."
Suì shè zhī. Thereupon he pardoned him.
Míng rì chū xíng guó, The next day he went out to travel the state,
shǐ wèi yòu, and made him (Xiǎn Zhēn 顯臻) his right-hand man.
Xī rán Jìn guó jiē ān. And so the whole state of Jìn 晉 was pacified.
Yǔ yuē: There is a saying:
「Huán Gōng rèn qí zéi ér Wén Gōng yòng qí dào.」 "Duke Huán 任桓公 employed his enemy, while Duke Wén 文公 employed his thief."
Gù yuē: Therefore, it is said:
「Míng zhǔ rèn jì bù rèn nù, "An enlightened ruler employs strategy, not anger,
àn zhǔ rèn nù bù rèn jì; a foolish ruler employs anger, not strategy;
jì shèng nù zhě qiáng, he who conquers anger with strategy is strong,
nù shèng jì zhě wáng.」 he who conquers strategy with anger perishes."
Cǐ zhī wèi yě. This is what it means.
Níng Qī yù gān Qí Huán Gōng, Níng Qī 甯戚 wanted to seek an audience with Duke Huán of Qí 齊桓公,
qióngkùn wú yǐ zì jìn, but being impoverished and destitute, he had no way to advance himself.
Yúshì, Therefore,
wèi shānglǚ lìn chē yǐ shì Qí, he hired himself out to a merchant caravan, renting a cart to go to Qí.
Mù sù yú guō mén zhī wài. At dusk, he lodged outside the city gate.
Huán Gōng jiāo yíng kè, Duke Huán was in the suburbs welcoming guests,
yè kāi mén pì lìn chē zhě, and at night, the gates were opened for those who rented carts,
zhí huǒ shèn shèng, holding torches in great abundance,
cóng zhě shèn zhòng. with many followers.
Níng Qī fàn niú yú chē xià, Níng Qī was feeding his ox beneath the cart,
wàng Huán Gōng ér bēi, gazing at Duke Huán and feeling sorrow,
jī niú jiǎo, he struck the ox's horn,
jí shāng gē. and sang a mournful merchant's song with urgency.
Duke Huán heard of it,
and, stroking the hand of his servant, said:
"How extraordinary!
This singer is no ordinary person."
He ordered that he be loaded into the rear carriage.
Duke Huán returned,
and his attendants used this to request (something).
Duke Huán said:
"Bestow upon him clothes and a hat,
and I will meet with him."
Níng Qī met him,
and persuaded Duke Huán about unifying the territory within.
The next day he met him again,
and persuaded Duke Huán about (ruling) all under Heaven.
Duke Huán was greatly pleased,
and was about to appoint him.
The assembled ministers argued against it, saying:
"He is a guest,
a person from Wèi,
distant from Qí by five hundred *lǐ*,
not far.
It would be better to send someone to inquire about him.
If he is indeed a worthy person,
appointing him will not be too late."
Duke Huán said:
"That is not so.
Inquiring about him, I fear that he may have minor faults.
Because of his minor faults,
To forget the great qualities of others
is how a ruler loses the scholars of the world.
Moreover, it is inherently difficult for a person to be perfect;
focus on employing their strengths."
Thereupon he promoted him,
greatly employed him,
and appointed him to be a high minister.
It was because of this promotion
that Duke Huán obtained him,
and this is how he became a hegemon.
Duke Huán of Qí sought an audience with the minor official Jì,
visiting three times in one day,
but was unable to see him.
His attendants said:
"The lord of ten thousand chariots,
for a commoner scholar,
visits three times in one day,
but is not able to see him,
perhaps you should stop."
Duke Huán said:
"No,
a scholar who is arrogant toward rank and emolument
naturally looks down on his lord;
a lord who is arrogant toward hegemons and kings
also looks down on his scholars.
Even if the master is arrogant toward rank and emolument,
How dare I be arrogant towards the Hegemon?"
He went five times before he was able to see him.
The world heard of this,
and they all said:
"Duke Huán still condescends to commoners,
how much more so would other rulers?"
Therefore,
they led each other to court,
none failed to arrive.
The reason why Duke Huán nine times united the feudal lords,
and rectified the empire once,
was because of how he treated men of virtue.
The "Book of Odes" says:
"Having illustrious virtue and conduct,
the four quarters of the empire will submit to him."
Duke Huán truly cherished this!
Marquis Wèi Wén passed by the lane of Duàn Gānmù and leaned on the railing of his carriage.
His servant said:
"Why do you lean on the railing, sir?"
He said:
"Is this not the lane of Duàn Gānmù?
Duàn Gānmù is indeed a worthy man,
how dare I not lean on the railing?
Moreover, I have heard that Duàn Gānmù has never been willing to trade himself for me,
how dare I esteem myself above him?
Duàn Gānmù is illustrious in virtue,
Guǎrén guāng hū dì; [My] insignificant person [values] land;
Duàn Gānmù fù hū yì, [Duàn] Gānmù values righteousness,
guǎrén fù hū cái; [my] insignificant person values wealth;
dì bùrú dé, land is not as good as virtue,
cái bùrú yì. wealth is not as good as righteousness.
Guǎrén dāng shì zhī zhě yě." [My] insignificant person should take this as a lesson."
Suì zhì lù bǎi wàn ér shí wǎng wèn zhī. Thereupon, he bestowed upon him a salary of a million and frequently went to inquire after him.
Guórén jiē xǐ, The people of the state were all pleased,
xiāng yǔ sòng zhī yuē: and together recited:
"Wú jūn hǎo zhèng, "Our lord loves uprightness,
Duàn Gānmù zhī jìng; [Duàn] Gānmù is respected;
wú jūn hǎo zhōng, our lord loves loyalty,
Duàn Gānmù zhī lóng." [Duàn] Gānmù is honored."
Jū wú jǐhé, After living for not too long,
Qín xīngbīng yù gōng Wèi. Qín raised an army wanting to attack Wèi.
Sīmǎ Tángqiě jiàn Qín jūn yuē: Sīmǎ Tángqiě advised the ruler of Qín, saying:
"Duàn Gānmù, "[Duàn] Gānmù,
xiánzhě yě, is a worthy man,
ér Wèi lǐ zhī, and Wèi respects him,
tiānxià mò bù wén, the whole world has heard of it,
wú nǎi bùkě jiā bīng hū?" might it not be inadvisable to add soldiers [attack]?"
Qín jūn yǐ wéi rán, The ruler of Qín thought so,
nǎi àn bīng ér chuò bù gōng. and then ordered the army to halt and cease the attack.
Wèi Wénhóu kěwèi shàn yòngbīng yǐ. Wèi Wénhóu can be said to be good at using the military.
Fú jūnzǐ shàn yòngbīng yě, Truly, a gentleman is good at using the military,
bù jiàn qí xíng, not seeing its form [manifestation],
ér gōng yǐ chéng, and the attack is already accomplished,
qí cǐ zhī wèi yě. that is what is meant by this.
The barbarian's use of soldiers
has drum sounds like thunder,
shouts that shake the earth,
dust filling the sky,
arrows flying like rain,
supporting the wounded and carrying the dead,
stepping on intestines and wading through blood.
The innocent people,
their dead already filling the marshes,
and yet the survival or destruction of the state,
the life or death of the ruler,
is still unknown.
They are far removed from benevolence and righteousness.
King Zhāo of Qín asked Sūn Qīng, saying:
"Scholars (Confucians) are of no benefit to a state."
Sūn Qīng said:
"Scholars emulate the former kings,
elevate ritual propriety and righteousness,
are careful in their conduct as ministers and sons,
and are able to cause their superiors to be respected.
If a ruler employs them,
then they advance in the court;
if they are placed aside and not employed,
then they retreat and become ordinary people, opposing [evil],
and will surely submit to those below.
Even if impoverished and suffering from cold and hunger,
bì bù yǐ xié dào wèi shí.
(they) have no place to stand an awl,
yet are clear about upholding the great plans of the state.
(Even though) they may shout but no one responds to them,
(they) are versed in regulating the myriad things and nourishing the people's livelihoods.
If (their) power is above others,
then (they) are the talent of kings and dukes;
if (their power) is below others,
then (they) are ministers of the state,
treasures of the ruler.
Even if they are hidden in humble dwellings and leaky houses,
no one does not value them,
because the Way truly resides within them.
When Zhòng Ní was the Minister of Crime in Lǔ,
Shěn Yóu Shì did not dare to drink his soup in the morning,
Gōng Shèn Shì divorced his wife,
Shèn Kuì Shì fled the territory.
Those selling cattle and horses in Lǔ did not preemptively set prices,
(but) set out the tax regulation to await (buyers).
(When he) resided in Quē Dǎng,
the children of Quē Dǎng used nets and snares,
and when dividing (the catch), those with relatives took more;
(but) he transformed them with filial piety and brotherly love.
If Confucian scholars are in the imperial court,
then (there is) beautiful governance;
if they are in lower positions,
then (there are) beautiful customs.
Such is the way of Confucians when they are subordinates."
The King said:
"Then,
what should one be like to be a ruler?"
Sūn Qīng replied, saying:
"One should be broad and great as a person.
One's will and intentions should be firm within,
proper etiquette should be cultivated in the court,
laws and measures should be correct in the government,
loyalty, trustworthiness, love, and benefit should manifest to those below.
To commit one injustice,
to kill one innocent person,
in order to gain the world,
he would not do it.
If righteousness and trustworthiness towards the people are established,
reaching the four seas,
then those beyond the world,
will respond to him and cherish him.
Why is this?
Then the noble name will be clear, and the world will be governed.
Therefore, those nearby will sing and praise him,
those far away will hurry to him with all their might,
those within the four seas will be like one family,
and all who are intelligent will submit.
This is what is meant by a teacher of men.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'From west, from east,
from south, from north,
there is no one who does not submit.'
This is what it means.
If being subordinate is like that,
and being a superior is like this,
how could he not be beneficial to the state?"
Zhāo Wáng said:
"Good!"
Tián Zàn, wearing Confucian robes, was received by the King of Jīng.
The King of Jīng said:
"Sir's clothes,
how ugly they are!"
Zàn replied:
"There are clothes even uglier than these."
The King of Jīng said:
"May I be permitted to hear about them?"
He replied:
"Armor is uglier than these."
The King said:
"What do you mean?"
He replied:
"In winter it is cold,
in summer it is hot,
no clothing is uglier than armor.
Zàn is poor,
therefore his clothes are ugly.
Now, Your Majesty,
is the ruler of ten thousand chariots,
"You are wealthy and unrivaled,
yet you are fond of clothing others in armor.
Your servant secretly considers this unacceptable for the Great King.
Could it be for its righteousness?
Matters of armor and weapons
split men's heads,
cut open men's bellies,
destroy men's cities,
capture men's children,
its reputation is especially dishonorable.
Could it be for its nobility?
If one is concerned with harming others,
others will surely be concerned with harming him;
if one is concerned with endangering others,
others will surely be concerned with endangering him.
Such nobility
is very unsettling to people.
These two things
are unacceptable for the Great King."
King Jīng was unable to respond.
Formerly, Duke Líng of Wèi asked about battle formations,
and Confucius spoke of ritual vessels,
devaluing warfare and valuing propriety.
Now, the Confucian robes
are the clothing of former kings,
yet King Jīng detests them;
weapons
are ill-omened instruments of the state,
And the King of Jīng was pleased with it.
The reason why he was humiliated by Tián Zàn and endangered his state was
why the "Spring and Autumn Annals" says:
"One who is good at governing a state does not employ the army."
This is what it means.
Duke Āi asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:
"I have heard that
expanding a dwelling to the east is inauspicious.
Is there any truth to this?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"There are five kinds of inauspiciousness,
but expanding to the east is not among them.
To harm others to benefit oneself
is inauspicious for the person;
to abandon the old and take the young
is inauspicious for the family;
to dismiss the worthy and employ the unworthy
is inauspicious for the state;
for the old not to teach
and for the young not to learn
is inauspicious for the customs;
for the sages to remain hidden
is inauspicious for the world.
Therefore, there are five kinds of inauspiciousness,
but expanding to the east is not among them.
The "Book of Poetry" says:
"Each reveres your ceremonies,
Heaven's mandate does not recur."
I have not heard of Dōngyě Bì being involved with fate."
5.13 Yán Yuān was attending Lǔ Dìnggōng on a terrace,
Yán Yuān was attending Duke Dìng of Lǔ on a terrace,
Dōngyě Bì was driving the horses below the terrace.
Dìnggōng said:
"Excellent!
Dōngyě Bì's driving."
Yán Yuān said:
"Good, it is good!
However,
his horses will soon falter."
Dìnggōng was displeased and
said to those around him:
"I have heard that
a gentleman does not slander people.
Does a gentleman also slander people?"
Yán Yuān was displeased,
went down the steps and left.
Shortly after,
the news of the horses' collapse arrived.
Dìnggōng kicked aside his mat and stood up, saying:
"Quickly, have someone invite Yán Yuān."
Yán Yuān arrived,
and Dìnggōng said:
"Just now, I said:
“Excellent!
Dōngyě Bì 御 (Yù) is truly a skilled charioteer."
Wú Zǐ said:
"Good, indeed it is good!
However,
his horses will be lost."
Someone asked: "I don't understand how you, a gentleman, know this?"
Yán Yuān said:
"Your servant knows it through principles of governance.
In the past,
Shùn was skilled at employing people,
Zàofù was skilled at employing horses.
Shùn did not exhaust his people,
Zàofù did not completely deplete his horses.
Therefore, Shùn did not lose his people,
Zàofù did not lose his horses.
Now, Dōngyě Bì's driving
when he mounts the chariot and grasps the reins,
his posture is correct;
his turns and paces,
his morning rituals are all complete;
he traverses dangers and seeks to go far,
and the horses' strength is exhausted.
Yet he continues to demand without end,
therefore I know they will be lost."
Duke Dìng said:
"Good,
can you elaborate a little further?"
Yán Yuān said:
"When a beast is cornered, it will butt;
when a bird is cornered, it will peck;
when a person is cornered, they will deceive.
From ancient times until now,
if those who are impoverished and beneath others can avoid danger,
there has never been such a case.
The *Book of Odes* says:
'Holding the reins like silk cords,
the two trace horses move as if dancing.'
This speaks of skillful driving."
Dìng Gōng said:
"Excellent!
It is my fault."
Kǒng Zǐ went north to the Shān Róng tribe.
There was a woman crying on the road,
and her crying was very mournful.
Kǒng Zǐ stopped his carriage and asked,
"Why do you cry so mournfully?"
The woman replied,
"Last year a tiger ate my husband,
and this year a tiger ate my son;
this is why I am grieving."
Kǒng Zǐ said,
"Alas!
If that is so,
"Then why don't you leave?"
He replied:
"Its government is fair,
its officials are not harsh,
it is because of this that I cannot leave."
Kǒngzǐ turned to Zǐgòng and said:
"Disciples, remember this,
a government that is unfair and officials who are harsh
are worse than tigers and wolves.
The *Shī* says:
'Bringing down death and famine,
cutting down and attacking the four regions,'
a government that is unfair
cuts down and attacks the four regions,
how much more so two people?
It is right that they do not leave!"
5.15 Wèi Wénhóu asked Lǐ Kè,
Wèi Wénhóu asked Lǐ Kè:
"What was the reason for the downfall of Wú?"
Lǐ Kè replied:
"Frequent battles and frequent victories."
Wénhóu said:
"Frequent battles and frequent victories
are a blessing for a state.
The reason for its downfall,
what is it?"
Lǐ Kè said:
"Frequent battles exhaust the people,
frequent victories make the ruler arrogant.
To rule an exhausted people with an arrogant ruler,
this is the reason for their downfall."
Therefore, those who love war and exhaust their armies
have never not perished.
Zhào Xiāngzǐ 赵襄子 asked Wángzǐ Wéi 王子維, saying:
"What was the reason for the downfall of Wú 吴?"
He replied:
"The ruler of Wú 吴 was *ài* 𠫤 (stingy) and unfeeling."
Xiāngzǐ 襄子 said:
"It is fitting!
That Wú 吴 perished.
Being stingy, he cannot reward the worthy;
being unfeeling, he cannot punish the wicked.
If the worthy are not rewarded,
and crimes cannot be punished,
what is he waiting for other than downfall?"
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 was sitting in attendance to Jì Sūn 季孫,
the steward of Jì Sūn 季孫 reported, saying:
"The ruler has sent someone to borrow a horse;
should we give it to him?"
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said:
"I have heard that taking from a subject
It is called taking,
not called borrowing."
Jìsūn understood,
and told the steward, saying:
"From now on,
when the ruler takes something,
call it taking,
do not call it borrowing."
Therefore, Confucius rectified the name of "borrowed horse,"
and the righteousness between ruler and subject was established.
The *Analects* says:
"What is necessary is to rectify names."
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Do not change your words lightly,
do not say 'it's alright'."
How can one not be careful?
The gentleman said:
"The Son of Heaven dwells within the palace gates,
inside curtains and screens,
beneath broad halls,
on felt carpets,
without leaving the tent,
yet knows the world,
because he has worthy assistants.
Therefore, seeing alone is not as clear as seeing with many,
hearing alone is not as discerning as hearing with many."
5.19 Duke Ping of Jin asked Shu Xiang,
"What is the greatest trouble of a state?"
He replied,
"That high officials value their great salaries and do not offer the most earnest advice,
that close officials fear punishment and dare not speak,
and that the feelings of those below are not communicated above --
these are the greatest troubles."
The Duke said,
"Good!"
So he issued an order to the state:
"If anyone wishes to offer good advice,
but the messengers do not pass it on,
the crime will be punishable by death!"
5.20 In Chu there was a man skilled at judging people's characters,
and his judgments never missed the mark,
which became known throughout the state.
King Zhuang saw him and inquired about his methods,
and he replied,
"Your servant is not skilled at judging people's characters,
but rather at observing their associations.
If a commoner
has associates who are all filial and fraternal,
are earnest and respectful, and fear the laws,
then that person's family will surely become more prosperous day by day,
and he himself will surely live in peace day by day;
Their family will surely prosper day by day,
their person will surely be at peace day by day.
This is what is called a "lucky person."
An official
is one who serves the ruler.
All their associates are sincere and trustworthy,
and they have a love of goodness.
Such a person
will be more and more helpful to the ruler,
and their official position will advance day by day.
This is what is called a "lucky official."
If the ruler is enlightened and the ministers are virtuous,
and those around him are mostly loyal,
and if the ruler has shortcomings,
they all dare to argue and offer correct remonstrations,
such a situation means that
the state will be at peace day by day,
the ruler will be honored day by day,
and the world will be wealthy day by day.
This is what is called a "lucky ruler."
"I am not able to judge people's characters,
but I am able to observe the company they keep."
King Zhuāng said:
"Excellent!"
Therefore,
he recruited men of talent from all directions,
diligently day and night,
and thus obtained men like Sūn Shū'áo and the general Zǐ Zhòng,
In order to prepare for ministers and prime ministers,
then to achieve hegemonic achievements.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"How numerous are the officers,
King Wén brought them peace."
This is what it means.
5.21 King Mǐn of Qí fled and lived in Wèi,
walking on foot during the day,
and said to Gōngyù Dān:
"I have already fled,
but I do not know the reason.
What is the reason for my fleeing?"
Gōngyù Dān replied:
"Your servant thought that Your Majesty already knew it,
but Your Majesty still doesn't know it?
The reason for Your Majesty's fleeing
is because of your virtue;
it is because the rulers of the world are all unworthy,
and they hate Your Majesty's virtue,
so they joined forces to attack Your Majesty,
this is the reason for Your Majesty's fleeing."
King Mǐn sighed deeply and said:
"Is virtue really this bitter?"
Dān again said to King Mǐn:
"The ancients had those who resigned from the world without a worried expression;
your servant has heard their voices,
And the king saw the truth of it.
The king called himself the Eastern Emperor,
and in reality possessed the empire.
He left his state to reside in Wèi,
his appearance was full and radiant,
his complexion glowing,
and he showed no desire to return to his country."
The king said,
"Excellent.
Dān knows that I, your servant, have benefited in three ways since I left my state to reside in Wèi."
Thereupon he became self-satisfied,
and his arrogance and self-importance knew no bounds.
King Mǐn fled to Wèi.
The lord of Wèi avoided his palace and lodged him elsewhere,
declared himself his subject, and provided him with necessities.
King Mǐn was not respectful,
so the people of Wèi attacked him.
King Mǐn then fled to Zōu and Lǔ,
displaying an arrogant manner.
Zōu and Lǔ did not accept him,
so he fled to Jǔ.
Chǔ sent Nào Chǐ to lead troops to rescue Qí,
and he subsequently became chancellor to King Mǐn.
Nào Chǐ severed King Mǐn's sinews,
and hung him from the temple rafters.
After a single night, he killed him,
and together with Yàn divided the territory of Qí.
Alas!
Mǐn Gōng, ruling over the great state of Qí,
with a territory of several thousand *lǐ*,
yet suffered military defeat at the hands of the various lords,
and territory was seized by Yān Zhāo,
ancestral temples were destroyed,
the altars of soil and grain were no longer sacrificed to,
palaces and houses were empty,
his person fled and escaped,
even worse than a common slave,
yet he still did not understand the reason for his downfall,
how truly lamentable!
He still considered himself worthy,
how could this not be sorrowful!
Gōngyù Dān, from among the slaves,
but his way of flattery and sycophancy
was extreme!
King Mǐn did not realize this,
pursued and favored him,
taking disgrace as honor,
taking worry as joy,
his demise was long overdue,
and eventually he was killed.
Before this,
Jìng Guō Jūn cruelly injured his people,
harmed and wounded his ministers,
the people of the state were about to betray and jointly expel him,
his charioteer knew this,
Prepared provisions in advance.
When the rebellion arose,
Lord Jing Guo fled,
arriving in the wilderness and becoming hungry.
His driver took out the provisions he had packed and offered them.
Lord Jing Guo said:
"How did you know to prepare provisions?"
He replied:
"Your Lordship's tyranny has been plotted by your ministers for a long time!"
qí chénxià zhī móu jiǔ yǐ!"
Lord Jing Guo angrily refused to eat,
saying:
"My reputation for virtue is widely known,
how can you call me tyrannical?"
His driver, fearing, said:
"Your servant spoke wrongly.
Your Lordship is truly virtuous,
it is only that the ministers are unworthy,
and together they harm the virtuous."
Then Lord Jing Guo was pleased,
and then he ate.
Therefore, King Min of Qi and Lord Jing Guo, even unto death,
never understood,
how sad!
5.22 Duke Zhao of Song fled,
arriving in a remote village,
With a sigh, he lamented,
"I know the reason for my downfall.
My courtiers number a thousand,
in enacting policies and recommending officials,
none does not say, 'My lord is a sage.'
My attendants number several hundred,
standing in their attire,
none does not say, 'My lord is beautiful.'
Within and without, I hear no faults of mine,
and that is why I have come to this."
Judging from the ruler of Sòng,
the reason why rulers become separated from their states and lose their altars of soil and grain
is that there are too many flatterers.
Therefore, Zhāo of Sòng, even in his downfall, was able to awaken,
and perhaps he was able to return to his state.
When Hú Hài, the Second Emperor of Qín, was still a young master,
he had several brothers.
An edict ordered a banquet with wine to entertain the assembled ministers,
and the various sons were summoned.
After the sons were granted food, they departed first.
Hú Hài descended the stairs,
observed which of the assembled ministers had well-made shoes on display,
and then proceeded to deliberately trample and ruin them before leaving.
All the sons who heard and saw this
could not help but sigh.
When the Second Emperor ascended the throne,
All knew that the world would surely abandon him.
Therefore, Èr Shì 二世 was deluded by Zhào Gāo 趙高,
slighted great ministers,
and did not care for the common people.
Because of this, Chén Shèng 陳勝 raised his arm in revolt east of the pass,
and Yán Yuè 閻樂 stirred up rebellion at Wàngyí 望夷.
Yán Yuè 閻樂,
was Zhào Gāo’s 趙高 son-in-law,
and served as the magistrate of Xiányáng 咸陽.
He falsely claimed to be pursuing bandits,
and led officers and soldiers into Wàngyí 望夷 palace,
attacking and shooting Èr Shì 二世.
He then enumerated Èr Shì’s 二世 crimes,
and intended to add the blade (i.e., kill him).
Èr Shì 二世 was afraid,
and went inside intending to kill himself.
There was a eunuch who followed him.
Èr Shì 二世 said,
"How did it come to this?"
The eunuch said,
"I have known this for a long time!"
Èr Shì 二世 said,
"Why didn't you say so earlier?"
He replied,
"It is because I didn't speak that
I was able to get to this point;
if I had spoken,
I would have been dead long ago."
然後二世喟然悔之， Then Èr Shì sighed and regretted it,
遂自殺。 and subsequently committed suicide.
「忠臣之事君也， "How should a loyal minister serve his ruler?"
齊侯問於晏子曰： Qí Hóu asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
何若？」 What should it be like?"
對曰： Yàn Zǐ replied:
「有難不死， "When there is calamity, he does not die;
出亡不送。」 when there is exile, he does not accompany him."
君曰： The ruler said:
「列地而與之， "I have apportioned land to give to him,
疏爵而貴之， I have bestowed titles to ennoble him.
君有難不死， If the ruler is in trouble and he doesn't die,
出亡不送， and if the ruler is exiled and he doesn't accompany him,
可謂忠乎？」 can this be called loyalty?"
對曰： Yàn Zǐ replied:
「言而見用， "If my words are heeded and employed,
終身無難， and I have no trouble for my entire life,
臣奚死焉？ why should I die?
諫而見從， If my advice is followed,
終身不亡， and I am not exiled for my entire life,
臣奚送焉？ why should I accompany him?
若言不見用， If my words are not heeded,
有難而死， and I die in calamity,
是妄死也； that would be a senseless death.
諫不見從， If my advice is not followed,
出亡而送， and I accompany him in exile,
This is a pretense.
Therefore, a loyal minister,
is able to bring complete goodness to the ruler,
but is not able to share being trapped in difficulty."
Sòng Yù 宋玉 through his friend was able to be presented to King Xiāng of Chǔ 楚襄王,
King Xiāng treated him no differently.
Sòng Yù blamed his friend,
his friend said:
"Ginger and cinnamon grow because of the land,
but are not spicy because of the land;
a woman marries because of a matchmaker,
but is not intimate because of the matchmaker.
Your service to the king has not yet begun,
why do you blame me?"
Sòng Yù said:
"Not so!
Formerly, in Qí 齊 there was a fine hare named Dōngguō Jū 东郭㕙,
which in a single day could run five hundred *lǐ*.
Therefore,
in Qí there was a fine dog named Hán Lú 韩卢,
which also in a single day could run five hundred *lǐ*.
If one makes them see each other from afar and points them towards each other,
then even Hán Lú cannot catch up to the dust of the many hares;
if one follows the tracks and unleashes the leash,
then even Dōngguō Jū cannot escape.
Now, how do you recommend me,
Is it by stepping on their tracks that one restrains them with ropes?
Is it by seeing them from afar that one points and commands them?
The *Book of Odes* says:
"Seeking ease, seeking joy,
they abandon me as if I were something lost."
This is what I mean."
His friend said:
"This servant has erred,
this servant has erred!"
Sòng Yù served King Xiāng of Chǔ but was not noticed.
His ambition was not realized,
manifesting in his countenance.
Someone said to him:
"Why is your discourse not praised,
and your plans doubted?"
Sòng Yù said:
"Not so!
Have you not seen the black monkey?
When it dwells in the forests of Guìlín,
atop steep leaves,
leisurely playing,
soaring back and forth,
stirring like a dragon and gathering like birds,
sadly whistling and long singing,
at such a time,
even Yì and Féng Méng
不得正目而視也。 > One cannot even look straight ahead.
及其在枳棘之中也， > And when it is among the brambles and thorns,
恐懼而掉慄， > it is fearful and trembles,
危視而蹟行， > cautiously looking around as it moves its tracks,
眾人皆得意焉。 > and everyone is pleased with it.
此皮筋非加急而體益短也， > This is not because the leather rope has been tightened further, making the body shorter;
處勢不便故也。 > it is because its position is inconvenient.
夫處勢不便， > If its position is inconvenient,
豈可以量功校能哉？ > how can one measure its merit and assess its ability?
《詩》不云乎？ > Does not the *Shī* say?
『駕彼四牡， > "Driving those four stallions,
四牡項領。』 > the four stallions strain their necks."
夫久駕而長不得行， > If they are driven for a long time and still cannot proceed far,
項領， > Straining their necks,
不亦宜乎？ > is it not fitting?
《易》曰： > The *Yì* says:
『臀無膚， > "The buttocks have no skin,
其行趑趄』， > and his gait is unsteady."
此之謂也。」 > This is what it means."
Tián Ráo 事 Lǔ Āi Gōng, > Tián Ráo served Lǔ Āi Gōng,
而不見察， > but was not recognized.
Tián Ráo 謂 Lǔ Āi Gōng 曰： > Tián Ráo said to Lǔ Āi Gōng:
「臣將去君而鴻鵠舉矣！」 > "Your servant will leave you, and the swan will take flight!"
Āi Gōng 曰： > Āi Gōng said:
「何謂也？」 > "What do you mean?"
Tián Ráo 曰： > Tián Ráo said:
"Has your lord not seen a rooster?
The one that wears a crown on its head,
is refined;
the one that has spurs on its feet,
is martial;
the one that dares to fight when an enemy is before it,
is brave;
the one that calls out when it sees food,
is benevolent;
the one that guards the night and does not miss the time,
is trustworthy.
Although the rooster possesses these five qualities,
your lord still boils it every day and eats it.
Why?
Because it comes from nearby.
A swan takes flight a thousand *lǐ*,
and stops in your lord's garden pond,
eating your fish and turtles,
pecking at your beans and grains,
and possessing none of these five qualities,
yet your lord still values it,
because it comes from afar.
I, your servant, ask to take flight like a swan!"
Āi Gōng said:
"Stop!
I will write down your words."
Tián Ráo said:
"I have heard that one who eats from a vessel
One who does not destroy his tools;
one who seeks shade under a tree,
does not break its branches.
If you have a scholar but do not employ him,
what is the point of recording his words?"
Thereupon, he left to go to Yān (燕),
where Yān (燕) appointed him as prime minister.
After three years,
the government of Yān (燕) was greatly peaceful,
and there were no thieves in the state.
Āi Gōng (哀公) heard of this,
and sighed deeply,
avoiding his bedchamber for three months,
and reducing his fine clothing,
saying:
"Not being careful at the beginning,
and regretting it afterward,
how can it be recovered?"
The *Shī* (詩) [Book of Odes] says:
"I will leave you,
and go to that pleasant land,
go to that pleasant land,
where I will find my place."
The *Chūnqiū* (春秋) [Spring and Autumn Annals] says:
"If one is younger than the ruler,
then the ruler will treat him lightly,"
this is what it means.
Zǐ Zhāng 子張 met with Duke Āi of Lǔ 魯哀公.
After seven days, Duke Āi did not treat him with courtesy.
He entrusted a servant and departed, saying:
"I have heard that the lord cherishes scholars.
Therefore, I did not consider it far, even though it was thousands of miles away.
I braved the frost and dew,
endured the dust and dirt,
travelled a hundred stages with doubled calluses,
and dared not rest in order to see the lord.
Yet, after seven days, the lord has not treated me with courtesy.
The lord's cherishing of scholars
is similar to Lord Yè Gōng Zǐ Gāo 葉公子高's love of dragons.
Yè Gōng Zǐ Gāo loved dragons.
He used hooks to depict dragons,
he used chisels to depict dragons,
and he decorated his house with carvings depicting dragons.
Thereupon, a real dragon heard of it and descended.
It peeked its head through the window
and extended its tail into the hall.
Yè Gōng saw it,
abandoned everything and fled,
losing his spirit,
his face drained of color.
This shows that Yè Gōng did not truly love dragons,
but rather loved things that resembled dragons but were not real dragons.
Now, I have heard that the lord cherishes scholars,
therefore I did not consider it far, even though it was thousands of miles away, to see the lord.
If for seven days you show no courtesy,
then you, my lord, are not a lover of scholars,
but rather a lover of those who resemble scholars but are not.
The *Shī* says:
"In my heart I cherish it,
on what day shall I forget it?"
I dare to entrust this and depart."
5.29 Formerly,
Master Chǔqiū, at the age of seventy,
wearing a fur coat and rope belt,
went to see Lord Mèngcháng,
but wanting to rush forward, he could not advance.
Lord Mèngcháng said:
"Sir, you are old,
your years are advanced,
what can you teach me?"
Master Chǔqiū said:
"Alas!
Are you treating me as old?
Alas!
Are you asking me to chase after carriages and race horses?
To throw stones and jump distances?
To pursue elk and grapple with leopards and tigers?
I am already dead,
how can I have time to grow old?
Alas!
Are you asking me to deliver righteous words and confront the feudal lords?
To resolve doubts and settle hesitations?
I am just now beginning to grow strong,
what old age is there to speak of?"
Lord Mèngcháng hesitated, avoiding his seat,
his face showing a look of shame.
The *Shī* says:
"Old men murmur,
Young boys strut."
This means that old men wish to exhaust their plans,
but the young are arrogant and do not accept them.
This is why Qín Mùgōng was defeated in his army,
and why Yīn Zhòu lost the empire.
Therefore, the *Book of Documents* says:
"The words of the grey-haired
will have no errors."
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"May you, with long life, be tried."
Praising the use of old men's words to pacify the state.
In Qí, there was Lǘqiū Áng,
eighteen years old,
who stopped Xuān Wáng on the road and said:
"My family is poor, and my parents are old,
I wish to obtain a small position."
Xuān Wáng said:
"You are still young,
it is not yet possible."
Lǘqiū Áng replied,
"Not so!
In the past, there was Zhuānxū,
who governed the empire at the age of twelve;
Qín Xiàng Tuó,
who became a teacher to sages at the age of seven.
From this perspective,
I, Áng, am merely unworthy,
and no longer young."
King Xuān said,
"There has never been a colt of a cubit or an inch that could pull a heavy load and go far.
From this perspective,
a scholar can only be useful after his hair has turned white and his head has become bald."
Lǘqiū Áng said,
"Not so!
A foot has its shortcomings,
and an inch has its strengths.
Huáliú and lùjì,
are the finest horses in the world,
but if they are made to compete with wildcats in the space of a pot and stove,
their speed will probably not surpass that of the wildcats.
Yellow swans and white cranes
fly a thousand miles with a single flap,
but if they are made to compete with swallows and bats under the eaves of the hall,
within the house,
their dexterity will probably not surpass that of the swallows and bats.
Bìlǘ and Jùquè,
are the sharpest weapons in the world,
Striking a stone doesn't chip it,
stabbing a stone doesn't file it down;
even if you made it compete with a reed pipe in piercing an eye, causing blurred vision,
its convenience might not surpass that of the reed pipe.
From this, if we observe,
how is white hair falling from the head
different from that of Yǎng 卬?"
King Xuān 宣王 said:
"Excellent!
You have wise words;
why have I seen you so late?"
Yǎng 卬 replied,
"The clamorous sounds of chickens and pigs
drown out the sound of bells and drums;
clouds and haze filling the throat
obscure the brightness of the sun and moon.
With slanderers at one's side,
that is why you see me so late.
The *Shī* 《詩》 (Book of Odes) says:
'If you listen to honest words, you respond;
if you listen to slanderous words, you retreat.'
How could I advance?"
King Xuān 宣王 patted the carriage rail and said:
"I have been at fault."
Thereupon, he gave him a ride back together and employed him.
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said:
"The younger generation is to be regarded with awe;
how do we know that those who come after will not be as good as we are now?"
This is what it is referring to.
A man of Jīng (荊) named Biàn Hé (卞和) obtained an uncut jade and presented it to King Lì (厲王) of Jīng.
The king ordered the jade appraiser to examine it,
who said,
"It is a stone."
The king considered Hé (和) to be deceiving him,
and cut off his left foot.
King Lì (厲王) died,
and King Wǔ (武王) ascended the throne.
Hé (和) again presented the uncut jade to King Wǔ (武王).
King Wǔ (武王) ordered the jade appraiser to examine it,
who said,
"It is a stone."
Again, he considered it to be deception,
and cut off his right foot.
King Wǔ (武王) died,
and King Gòng (共王) ascended the throne.
Hé (和) then held the uncut jade and wept in the Jīng Mountains (荊山),
for three days and three nights.
He wept until his tears were exhausted, and he continued with blood.
King Gòng (共王) heard of this
and sent someone to ask him, saying,
"There are many in the world who have been punished.
Why do you alone weep so bitterly?"
He replied,
"To call precious jade a stone,
To execute a loyal man with deceit,
this is what your servant grieves about!"
Gòng Wáng said:
"What a pity,
that my late king listened!
It is difficult to cut open a stone, but easy to chop off a man's feet!
The dead cannot be brought back to life,
the severed cannot be rejoined,
what difference is there in listening?"
Then he sent men to work on the uncut jade and obtained the treasure.
Therefore, it was named Hé Shì's Bi (Hé's Jade Disc).
Thus it is said:
"Pearls and jade,
are what rulers value,
Hé, although he presented a beautiful treasure,
was not used by the jade craftsmen.
Presenting treasure is so difficult,
how much more difficult is it to present a worthy man?
Worthy men and treacherous ministers,
are like enemies,
whose intentions do not agree with mediocre rulers.
To make treacherous ministers recommend their enemies to a ruler whose intentions they don't agree with,
is ten thousand times more difficult than Hé Shì's Bi,
and there are no ministers with severed feet to exemplify its difficulty,
it is like uprooting a mountain.
Once in a thousand years they align,
walking in each other's footsteps,
and then a virtuous king arises.
Those who are virtuous but not employed,
are too many to count.
Therefore, the fact that those who possess the Dao are not killed,
is like a piece of unrefined jade that has not yet been presented."
Reproving Extravagance, Section Six.
6.1 Jié built the Yaotai terrace,
exhausting the strength of the people,
depleting the wealth of the people,
creating wine pools and dregs embankments,
indulging in decadent music,
with three thousand people drinking like oxen to the beat of a single drum.
The courtiers held each other and sang, saying:
"The Jiāng River is overflowing,
the boats and oars are ruined,
our king is deposed,
quickly return to Bó,
Bó is also large!"
And also said:
"Happy, happy,
the four stallions are strong,
the six reins are sleek,
abandon evil and follow good,
why not be happy!"
Yī Yǐn knew that Heaven's mandate was imminent,
raised his cup and said to Jié:
"If the ruler does not heed his minister's words,
"Ruin is not far off!"
Jié clapped his hands and rose,
and, laughing harshly, said:
"What sorcerous words are these you speak?
I possess the empire,
just as Heaven possesses the sun.
Can the sun perish?
If the sun perishes,
then I too shall perish!"
Thereupon,
he put on his shoes and departed,
and consequently went over to Tāng,
and Tāng established him as a minister.
Therefore, Yī Yǐn left his office and entered into service with the Yīn,
and the Yīn prospered while the Xià perished.
Zhòu constructed the Deer Terrace,
which took seven years to complete,
its size was three *lǐ*,
and its height was a thousand *chǐ*,
overlooking and watching clouds and rain.
He created the punishment of the burning pillar,
executing the innocent,
seizing the people's strength,
and inflicting injustice and violence upon the common people,
and cruel poison upon the high officials.
The whole world betrayed him,
I desire to be like Minister King Wén.
When the Zhōu army arrived,
his orders were not carried out by his attendants,
alas!
At that time,
to seek to be a commoner,
was not possible,
Zhòu brought it upon himself.
6.3 King Wèi was about to build the Central Celestial Terrace,
and ordered:
"Whoever dares to remonstrate shall die!"
Xǔ Wǎn carried a shovel and entered,
and said:
"I heard that the Great King is about to build the Central Celestial Terrace,
and I wish to add my strength."
The King said:
"What strength do you have to add?"
Wǎn said:
"Although I have no strength,
I can estimate the Shāng Terrace."
The King said:
"How so?"
He said:
"I have heard that the distance between heaven and earth
is fifteen thousand *lǐ*.
Now, if Your Majesty halves that distance,
(You) want to build a terrace of seven thousand five hundred *lǐ*.
Since the height is like this,
its base must be eight thousand *lǐ* square.
All of the king's land
is not enough to be the base of the terrace.
In ancient times, Yáo and Shùn established the feudal lords
with territories of five thousand *lǐ* square.
If the king insists on building this terrace,
he must first attack the feudal lords with soldiers,
seizing all their land.
Even then, it would not be enough.
Then, he must attack the four barbarian tribes,
obtaining eight thousand *lǐ* square,
which would then be enough to be the base of the terrace.
The accumulation of timber,
the multitude of laborers,
the storage in granaries,
would be counted in the tens of millions.
Beyond the eight thousand *lǐ*,
you must establish farmland
sufficient to provide for the king's terrace.
Once the terrace is fully prepared,
then it can be built."
King Wèi was silent and had nothing to say in response,
and then abandoned the construction of the terrace.
Duke Líng of Wèi was digging a pond because of the cold weather.
Wǎn Chūn remonstrated, saying:
"To begin labor in the cold weather
I fear, will harm the people."
The duke said:
"Is it cold?"
Wǎn Chūn said:
"Your Lordship wears fox-fur robes,
sits on a bear-skin mat,
and in the inner corner, there is a stove,
therefore you do not feel the cold.
But now the people's clothes are tattered and not mended,
their shoes are broken and not repaired,
your Lordship does not feel the cold,
but the people are truly cold."
The duke said:
"Good!"
He ordered the labor to cease.
Those around him remonstrated, saying:
"Your Lordship, in digging the pond,
did not know it was cold,
but because Wǎn Chūn knew, you ceased the labor.
This means virtue will be attributed to Wǎn Chūn,
and resentment will be directed at you, Lord."
The duke said:
"Not so!
Wǎn Chūn
is a commoner of the Lǔ state.
I promoted him,
The people have not seen it.
Now I will cause the people to see it because of this.
Moreover, spring also has goodness,
and I, the寡人 (guǎ rén), have it;
is the goodness of spring
not my goodness?"
Líng Gōng (靈公) discussing Wǎn Chūn (宛春),
can be said to have known the way of a ruler!
King Xuān (宣王) of Qí (齊) built a large hall,
roughly a hundred *mǔ* in size,
with three hundred households on the hall,
given the greatness of the state of Qí (齊),
it took three years to prepare for it but he was still unable to complete it,
and none of the ministers dared to remonstrate.
Xiāng Jū (香居) asked King Xuān (宣王), saying:
"The King of Jīng (荊王) abandoned the rites and music of the former kings,
and pursued excessive pleasures,
may I ask, does the state of Jīng (荊) have a ruler?"
The king said:
"It is as if there is no ruler."
"May I ask, does the state of Jīng (荊) have ministers?"
The king said:
"It is as if there are no ministers."
Jū (居) said:
"Now, Your Majesty is building a large hall,
and after three years it cannot be completed,
而群臣莫敢諫者， And none of the assembled ministers dared to remonstrate,
敢問王為有臣乎？」 Dare I ask, does Your Majesty consider himself to have any ministers?"
王曰： The king said:

His benevolence and kindness were generous,
